info.title: Yuvomi API
info.description: OpenAPI documentation for the Yuvomi family organizer backend.

get.description: Public bootstrap metadata for login/setup, including `product` and `client_api`, which let a client recognise an instance and tell whether it is new enough before anyone signs in. When a valid session or API token is supplied, the response also includes the exact app version and `max_upload_bytes`. A client probing an instance sends no credential: an invalid one answers 401.

Use `?download=1` to receive the OpenAPI document as a downloadable file.

Admin-only endpoint.

With two-factor authentication turned on, a right password opens no session yet: the response is `{ twoFactorRequired, recoveryAvailable }`, and POST /auth/2fa/verify completes the sign-in.

Deliberately does not reject existing sessions: in a household where nobody has set it up yet, that would lock everyone out, including the admin. Ends every browser session of the signed-in user except the calling one (#1354) and answers `{ ok: true, ended }` with the number of sessions ended. Only a browser session may call it: an API token or a wall display has no current session to keep and gets 403. API tokens and paired wall displays are not sessions and stay valid; revoke them under API tokens and Displays.

A refusal a user can reach carries a `reason` next to `error` (#1909): `browser_session_required` (403, only a signed-in browser session can sign out the other sessions, not an API token).

get.description: Public login-page bootstrap endpoint. Returns which ways in this server offers: whether OIDC is configured and enabled, and whether password login is allowed (AUTH_ALLOW_PASSWORD_LOGIN, ignored unless OIDC is fully configured). The login page waits for this single answer before painting, so it never shows a form that then disappears. guest_password_login_enabled is true only where password login is off AND the household actually has split-expense guests, who are exempt from the switch (#847) because they are external people with no account in the household identity provider. It is one bit and says nothing about who or how many; where password login is open the question is moot and the field is false.
Redirects the browser to the configured OIDC provider. State, nonce, and PKCE verifier are stored in the session.

302.description: Redirect to app or login error page

get.description: Consumes the OIDC callback, validates state/nonce/PKCE, creates or finds the linked user, establishes a session, and redirects back to the app. An identity without a linked account is matched by its verified email address against accounts not yet linked (split-expense guests excluded). It links only an account whose address nobody but an admin can have set: an account without a password (SSO-only) or an admin account. Two or more matching accounts redirect to /login?error=oidc_email_ambiguous; a single matching member account that has a password redirects to /login?error=oidc_link_required, and that member links SSO while signed in (POST /api/v1/auth/oidc/link/start). Neither case creates or links an account, whatever OIDC_ALLOW_SIGNUP says. With OIDC_ALLOW_SIGNUP=false an identity that matches no existing account is redirected to /login?error=oidc_signup_disabled instead of being provisioned. A link run started while signed in (POST /api/v1/auth/oidc/link/start) redirects to /settings/personal/account?oidc_linked=1, or on refusal to /settings/personal/account?oidc_link_error=<reason>: `user_gone` (the account no longer exists or can no longer sign in), `already_linked` (the account is linked to another identity), `sub_taken` (the identity is linked to another account).

post.description:
Unknown body fields are ignored. `language` and `timezone` are optional; servers before they were added ignore them as well. A rejected `timezone` answers 400 with `reason: "invalid_timezone"`, so a client can retry without the field; other validation errors carry no `reason`. Every failed request counts against the login rate limit.

A refusal a user can reach carries a `reason` next to `error` (#1909): `setup_completed` (403, setup has already been completed).

200.description: Generic acknowledgement (sent regardless of whether the account exists).

post.description: Always responds 200 with a generic body to prevent account enumeration. A reset email is sent only when the account exists, has a linked email, SMTP is configured, and BASE_URL is set. The response is sent before the account is looked up; the lookup and the email run afterwards in the background, so the response time does not reveal whether the account exists. An email address matches regardless of surrounding whitespace and capitalisation; if it belongs to more than one account, no email is sent (guests of shared expenses do not count towards that), so such accounts reset by username.

post.description: Public bootstrap endpoint for the /reset-password page. Shares the rate limit of POST /reset-password and never consumes the token. Unknown, expired and already used tokens, and tokens of an account that can no longer reset its password, all return valid: false, so the endpoint reveals nothing beyond whether the token can still be used. The token travels in the body, not the URL, so it stays out of access logs.

post.summary: Fetch the Gravatar for the calling account once and store it as the profile picture

200.description: The picture was stored; the updated account

400.description: The account has no single stored email address (`reason: "no_email"`)

403.description: The account is not a household member, e.g. a split-expense guest (`reason: "not_a_household_member"`); nothing is fetched. A paired wall display gets `reason: "display_account"`

404.description: The feature is not configured: `GRAVATAR_BASE_URL` is unset or empty (`reason: "gravatar_disabled"`), or the service has no picture for the address (`reason: "gravatar_not_found"`)

409.description: The `email` sent does not match the stored address (refused before anything is fetched), or the picture, the stored address or the account changed while the picture was being fetched; nothing was stored (`reason: "gravatar_stale"`)

415.description: The response is not a PNG, JPEG or WebP image, by type or by content (`reason: "gravatar_not_image"`)

429.description: More than 10 calls in 10 minutes for this account (`reason: "gravatar_rate_limited"`)

502.description: The service could not be reached: timeout, DNS, a target refused by the SSRF guard, or a non-2xx answer other than 404 (`reason: "gravatar_unreachable"`)

post.description: A one-shot import, not a live provider: the server hashes the account's stored email address (SHA-256 of the trimmed, ASCII-lowercased address), fetches the picture from the configured Gravatar base URL once (HTTPS only, at most five redirects, private network targets refused, 8 s timeout, at most 512 KiB of PNG, JPEG or WebP whose bytes match the declared type) and stores it exactly like an upload through `PATCH /api/v1/auth/me/profile`: into `avatar_data`, mirrored to the account's birthday photo. Nothing is fetched again later; a later upload overwrites the import and a later import overwrites the upload. Off unless the operator sets `GRAVATAR_BASE_URL` (nothing is sent while it is unset; `GET /api/v1/auth/me` reports `gravatarAvailable`). Self only and household members only; a paired wall display is refused like every other account write. If the picture, the address or the account changes while the fetch runs, nothing is stored (409). Only the hash, the server's IP and its User-Agent reach the service, never the address. Limited to 10 calls per account per 10 minutes.

get.description: Lists every account except wall displays: user administration, and the way clients name a person a record already stores. It is not a picker source: pickers read `GET /api/v1/family/members`. A deactivated account (see `DELETE /api/v1/auth/users/{id}`) stays in this list, sorted after the active ones, with `deactivated_at` set to the moment it was deactivated; the field is `null` for an active account. Within the active and within the deactivated accounts the list follows the household member order (see `GET /api/v1/family/members`): `sort_order` is the position of a household member, `null` for an unplaced member and for every account that is no household member; `is_household_member` tells the two apart. Administrators additionally get sso_only per member; how someone else signs in is not a detail every member needs, for the same reason the 2FA overview is a separate admin endpoint.

traces.description: Columns that reference the account from shared data. Empty when the account was deleted.

delete.description:
Removes an account. What that means depends on what the account leaves behind. An account with traces in shared data is DEACTIVATED: the row stays, so records keep their author, assignee and balances, and the answer carries `outcome: "deactivated"`. A trace is any row that references the account outside its own private data, for example a task, event, note or document it created, an assignment, a shared expense it paid, took part in or recorded, a quick link, or reward points. An account without traces is deleted as before (`outcome: "deleted"`), together with its private data. Deactivating ends every way in at once and in one transaction: sessions are ended, API tokens acting as the account or issued by it are revoked, open invitations and display pairing codes it created stop working, calendar feed addresses stop working, password and SSO sign-in are refused, pending password reset links are dropped, and push subscriptions, personal notification channels and pending reminders are removed. The role falls back to member. Private data of the account (health, cycle, private notes, shift plans, its contact card and birthday) is kept. A deactivated account is no household member any more: it is missing from `GET /api/v1/family/members` and cannot be newly chosen as assignee, attendee or group member, while references already stored stay valid. `traces` lists the referencing columns with their row counts. Refused with 400 and a `reason`: `own_account` (the caller's own account), `last_admin`, `last_sso_admin`. Wall displays are managed under `/api/v1/displays` and answer 404 here.

Admin-only endpoint.

get.description:
The caller's own devices that still count. No administrator can read another member's list. The device credential is never returned here.

A refusal a user can reach carries a `reason` next to `error` (#1909): `session_required` (403, an API token cannot read a person's devices).

201.description: Device added. The plaintext credential is returned only once.

post.description:
Exchanges a sign-in for a device credential, the bearer a native client uses from then on. A device acts as the person, with less reach than a browser session: an administrator is an ordinary member on it, and of `/api/v1/auth` it reaches only `GET /me`, `GET /users`, `GET /oidc/config`, `POST /logout`, `GET /devices` and `DELETE /devices/{id}`; anything else answers 403 with `reason: device_credential`. It ends after 90 days without use, and with everything that ends a session. The same `device_id` replaces the earlier credential.

A refusal a user can reach carries a `reason` next to `error` (#1909): `device_credential` (403, a device cannot add another device), `session_required` (403, an API token cannot add a device), `not_a_household_member` (403, the account is no household member).

201.description: Code created. It is returned only once.

post.description:
Creates a short code that signs a device in as the caller, for a household without passwords or a person who prefers not to type one. The code holds for five minutes and once, and a new code ends the previous one. The same code comes back three ways: plain to type, as a `yuvomi://pair` link for this device and as a QR code of that link for a second device. Only from a browser session.

A refusal a user can reach carries a `reason` next to `error` (#1909): `device_credential` (403, a device cannot create a pairing code), `session_required` (403, an API token cannot create one), `not_a_household_member` (403, the account is no household member).

201.description: Device added. The plaintext credential is returned only once.

post.description:
Exchanges a pairing code for a device credential. Public, the code is the proof. Send no `Authorization` header: a valid device credential is refused here. Unknown, expired and used codes answer alike, and so does the code of an account that can no longer have a device. Attempts are limited.

A refusal a user can reach carries a `reason` next to `error` (#1909): `invalid_pairing_code` (400, the code is unknown, expired, used, or its account can no longer have a device), `device_credential` (403, the request carried a valid device credential).

get.description: The image bytes of a profile picture (PNG, JPEG or WebP). List rows that show a person - `assigned_avatar` and `assigned_users[].avatar_data` on tasks and events, `creator_avatar` on notes, `worker_avatar_data` on housekeeping visits, `user_avatar`/`person_avatar` in the completion feed and `user_avatar` in the money ledger - carry this address (with a `v` query parameter, a random key that changes with every new picture and is required here) instead of a data URL, or `null` when the person has no picture. post.description:
A backup carries the encryption of the installation that wrote it. To restore an encrypted backup from ANOTHER installation, send that installation's DB_ENCRYPTION_KEY in `X-Backup-Key`: the backup is re-encrypted with this installation's own key, and the sent key is used only for this request and never stored. The key is accepted only in this header, never in the URL. If this installation's own key already opens the backup, the header is ignored. An installation without a DB_ENCRYPTION_KEY of its own refuses a backup key rather than storing the backup decrypted. Every 400 response may carry a machine-readable `reason`: `backup_key_required` (the backup does not open with this installation's key - send `X-Backup-Key`), `backup_key_wrong`, `backup_key_invalid` (header is not base64), `own_key_missing`, `backup_damaged`, `backup_unreadable`, `backup_corrupt` (the integrity check found damage in the backup file). A second restore while one is still running is refused with 409 and reason `restore_in_progress`. If syncs, backups or requests are still running after 60 seconds, the restore gives up without changing anything: 503 with reason `restore_busy`. A failed restore leaves this installation unchanged.

Admin-only endpoint.

200.description: The data of the overview. Depending on module access it can carry further fields that are not described here.

get.description: Aggregated data for every overview tile. Optional query parameters filter tasks, upcoming events and pinned notes before row limits and counts are computed. Task filters apply to every task slice (`urgentTasks`, `openTaskCount`, `overdueTaskCount`, `memberTodayTasks`, `tasksDoneToday`, `wallTasks`); note filters apply to `pinnedNotes`, `pinnedNotesCount` and `notesTotal` alike. Event filters apply to both `upcomingEvents` and `weekEvents` (the events touching the household days from yesterday to a week ahead, in a compact shape for the week strip of the calendar tile). The browser derives these filters from per-widget `options` stored in `dashboard_widgets`. `upcomingEvents` counts only appointments that have not ended toward its five-item cap; already ended ones of today (end before now in the household time zone, never all-day ones) come along outside the cap. `familyEvents` feeds the Family card: per household member the appointments of today (ended ones included) and the next coming ones, merged once; the `events_scope` filter does not apply to it, `events_birthdays` does. `wallTasks` feeds wall mode: per household member the tasks of today by title (`open`: not done and due today or earlier; `done`: done and due today, or overdue and ticked off today in the household time zone), at most six titles each next to the uncapped `open_count` and `done_count`. Unlike every other task slice it carries only tasks with visibility `all`, whoever the caller is: a wall tablet is not a person. `wastePickups` lists the collections of today and tomorrow (Waste module), `myShiftsToday` the own shifts of the caller of today (Schedule module); both are empty when the module is denied. `splitBalance` (`{ net, positions }`) lists what the caller has open in shared expenses: net per currency and each open position from the settle-up view of the caller's active groups (the same balances as `GET /split-expenses/groups/{id}/balances`), household currency first; it is empty without `budget` read access. A module the household has switched off (`disabled_modules` in `/preferences`) is left out the same way as a denied one: its fields stay in the response with their empty values. `birthdays` is a switch of its own here, so the birthday fields follow it rather than the `calendar` switch, and `upcomingEvents`, `weekEvents` and `familyEvents` carry no birthday events while it is off.

parameters.name: notes_category
parameters.description: Limit pinned notes to those carrying every selected category (AND). Repeatable positive category IDs, deduplicated and capped at 50. Omitted or empty means all visible pinned notes. Only household categories and the caller's own personal categories may match; another user's personal category cannot reveal notes.

parameters.name: tasks_category
parameters.description: Limit tasks to these categories. Repeatable; several values combine with OR. Omitted or empty means every category.

parameters.name: audience
parameters.description: `household` asks for the version for a shared surface (wall mode): an allowlist. The response then carries only the keys a wall draws: `users`, `upcomingEvents`, `birthdays`, `urgentTasks`, `tasksDoneToday`, `wallTasks`, `todayMeals`, `shoppingOpenCount`, `wastePickups`, of `pantryExpiring` the fields `todayItems` and `todayCount`, and of `housekeeping` the fields `present`, `presentSince` and `workerName`. Tasks and appointments in them are those the whole household may see - visibility `all`, appointments from ICS subscriptions only from shared ones - whoever the caller is, creator and assignees included; `events_scope=mine` is ignored. Every other key keeps its place in the same empty form as for a caller without the module - notes, `budget`, `splitBalance`, `quicklinks`, `countdowns`, the counters and week/family slices of tasks and calendar, `housekeeping.unpaidAmount`, and what belongs to the caller alone (`health`, `fasting`, `nutrition`, `myShiftsToday`, `rewards`); `shoppingTile` is absent. A key added to this response later is empty for this audience until it is put on the list. The parameter only narrows the response, so it needs no scope of its own. Anything else means the personal version.

parameters.name: events_scope
parameters.description: `mine` limits appointments to those assigned to the calling user - among the assignees, so an unassigned event is not "mine" (same reading as the calendar module). A paired display has no assignments of its own, so for it `mine` reads as all appointments. Anything else means all appointments.

parameters.name: events_birthdays
parameters.description: `hide` drops appointments that belong to a birthday entry from `upcomingEvents` and `weekEvents`, so a household that already shows the Birthdays tile does not read them twice. Applied before the cap (`events_limit`), so the freed rows are filled with the next real appointments. Anything else keeps them - birthdays are in by default.

parameters.name: shopping_list
parameters.description: Which lists the shopping tile shows. Repeatable positive list IDs, deduplicated and capped at 50. The selection applies to the tile only: with it the response carries an extra field `shoppingTile` = `{ lists, openCount, listCount }` - the selected lists (at most three, also those without open items, lists with open items first, each with up to six open items), the open items within the selection, and how many selected lists exist. `shoppingLists`, `shoppingOpenCount` and `shoppingOpenLists` are never affected and keep counting across all lists. IDs of lists that do not exist are dropped; when none of the IDs exists, or the value is not an ID, the request answers like one without the parameter and `shoppingTile` is absent. A caller without access to shopping gets the empty shopping payload and no `shoppingTile`.

parameters.name: events_calendar
parameters.description: Which calendars the appointments come from, under the keys of the calendar module: `local:<id>` for an own calendar, `cal:<id>` for a synced one (CalDAV, Google), `sub:<id>` for an ICS subscription - the `key` values of `sources` from `GET /calendar/calendars`, the catalogue the selection is checked against. Repeatable, deduplicated and capped at 50; a value of any other shape is dropped. Applies to `upcomingEvents` and `weekEvents` before the cap (`events_limit`), not to `familyEvents`. Appointments that belong to no calendar (birthdays, housekeeping visits) always pass; birthdays have `events_birthdays`. Keys the caller cannot choose (a deleted calendar, a removed subscription, a disconnected account, another member's private subscription) are dropped; when none is left the request answers like one without the parameter, never with an empty list.

parameters.name: events_limit
parameters.description: How many upcoming appointments `upcomingEvents` lists: `5`, `8` or `12`. The value is matched against exactly these three; anything else - omitted, empty, repeated, `7`, `500` - means `5`. Appointments of today that have already ended come on top and do not count against it. `weekEvents` and `familyEvents` are not affected.

Each entry carries both people: `user_id` is who ticked it off and `done_by_user_id` is who was named as having done it (#1205, null when nobody was), with `person_user_id` resolving the two into the one the entry displays. `source` is `null` for a completion in Yuvomi and `"caldav"` for one taken over by the inbound CalDAV sync when the task was ticked off in a reminders app (#1836); such an entry carries no person, since the sync cannot tell who ticked it off, and its time is the COMPLETED stamp of the reminder where it has one. Recording started with the release that introduced it, so nothing before that appears. Timestamps are UTC instants; which calendar day one belongs to is a question for the display timezone, which is why there is no date range here. Only tasks the caller may see are returned, evaluated live against the task - a task later set to private disappears from the history too. Subtasks are never recorded: a checklist item is part of its parent instruction, and the completion of the parent is the event.

Body: { order } with at most 500 task IDs (integers) in the wanted order. The list may be a subset of a category (an active filter, tasks the caller cannot see): the ranks the listed tasks already hold are sorted and dealt out again in the new order, tasks without a rank get new ranks behind the highest one in use, and every task not listed keeps its rank, so nothing collides. Body: { status, done_by_user_id? }. Sending `archived` files the task away without touching its status - use PATCH /archive instead. patch.summary: Decide a redemption (fulfill/reject/cancel) or take the decision back (reopen)
patch.description:
Body: { action: "fulfill" | "reject" | "cancel" | "reopen" }. REOPEN (R23) is the undo of a decision: only the account that decided may send it - for a fulfilment or rejection only an administrator, and never for a request fulfilled automatically at filing (`decided_by` equals `requested_by`; 403 `reason: "rewards_reopen_not_allowed"`), while whoever cancelled may reopen their own cancellation - within 10 minutes of the decision (later 409 `reason: "rewards_reopen_expired"`, an open request 409 `reason: "rewards_redemption_open"`). The request is pending again and the balance stands as before the decision: a fulfilled reward keeps its reserved points, a rejected or cancelled reward takes back exactly its `reversal` entry, a fulfilled money request drops its money entry. If the balance no longer allows that, the decision stays and the answer is 409 with `reason: "insufficient_points"` or `"insufficient_funds"`. Fulfilling a request whose reward has no units left does not fail silently: the request is REJECTED with `decision_reason: "out_of_stock"`, the reserved points go back through the usual `reversal`, and the answer is 409 with `reason: "out_of_stock"` and the decided row in `data`. Rejecting and cancelling stay untouched - sold out means only that fulfilling finds no unit. POCKET MONEY (#1734): fulfilling a withdrawal books the amount off the money balance, fulfilling a deposit credits it; rejecting and cancelling book nothing, because nothing was reserved. The cover is checked again when a withdrawal is fulfilled: if the balance no longer covers it, the answer is 409 with `reason: "insufficient_funds"` and the request STAYS pending. When a member is deactivated, their open money requests are cancelled with `decision_reason: "account_deactivated"`; fulfilling one that is still open for a deactivated member cancels it and answers 409 with `reason: "account_deactivated"`. A money request the caller may not read (somebody else's, for a non-administrator) answers 404 for every action, exactly like an id that does not exist.

get.summary: Pocket money accounts the caller may see
get.description: Answers { currency, minor_unit, accounts, candidates }. An account is { id, display_name, balance_minor, currency, minor_unit, former, closable, plan } with `plan` either null or { amount_minor, currency, minor_unit, frequency, anchor_day, next_run_date, paused }. AN ACCOUNT IS A ROW OF ITS OWN AND HAS EXACTLY ONE CURRENCY: the household currency of the day it was opened. The code is also written on every money entry, every money request and the plan. A later change of the household currency leaves existing accounts as they are - read `currency` and `minor_unit` (decimals per ISO 4217) from the ACCOUNT, not from the top level, which names the household currency a NEW account would be opened in. `closable` is true for an account with no plan, balance zero and nothing pending; only such an account can be closed, and one opened again takes the household currency of then. `former: true` marks the account of a deactivated member that still holds a balance; only administrators get it, it can only be paid out, and it leaves the list at balance zero. WHO SEES WHAT: a member gets their own account or an empty list, an administrator gets every account, a paired display gets none. A scoped API token follows the same rule through its subject and role. Pocket money is separate from points: there is no conversion in either direction. `candidates` lists the members without an account and is filled for administrators only.

put.summary: Create or change the scheduled credit of a member
put.description:
Body: { amount, frequency: "weekly" | "monthly", anchor_day, paused? }. `anchor_day` is the day of the month (1-31) for a monthly plan and the weekday (1 = Monday to 7 = Sunday) for a weekly one. A month without the anchor day takes its last day and the day comes back afterwards (31 -> 28/29 -> 31). Due dates missed while the server was off are booked afterwards, each exactly once; a paused plan books nothing and skips its missed dates when it is resumed. A plan whose member is no longer part of the household is paused instead of credited. Changing only the amount keeps the next date. Dates that are due when the plan is changed are booked first, with the plan as it was, in the same transaction as the change - a new amount or a new anchor day never reaches back. `paused` left out keeps the stored state: a paused plan stays paused. The plan keeps the currency of the account; an optional `currency` that differs is 400 with `reason: "currency_mismatch"`. The plan of a deactivated member stays paused: changing or resuming it is 409 with `reason: "account_deactivated"`. A single amount is limited to 10^12 minor units.

The picture of the cook is not repeated on every meal; it is on the member (`GET /api/v1/family/members`; a scoped token needs `family:read` for it, `meals:read` alone is refused there with 403). A meal of a weekly series also names the cook stored on the series as `recurrence_cook_user_id`, which can differ from its own.

A refusal a user can reach carries a `reason` next to `error` (#1909): `meals_selected_recipe_not_found` (400, the chosen `recipe_id` does not exist).

Only a household member can be chosen: housekeeping staff, split-expense guests, wall tablets and deactivated accounts are refused with 400, and an id that belongs to no account gets the same answer. A cook that is already stored on the meal stays valid; for `scope=series` that is the cook stored on the series.

repeat_until.description: Last date of the series; empty or missing means it never ends.

put.description:
Changes this meal alone. With `?scope=series` on a meal of a weekly series, the content fields are written to the series and to every meal created from it. `cook_user_id` follows the same choice: without `scope` it changes the cook of this meal and leaves the series untouched; with `scope=series` it reaches the series and all its meals. A missing `cook_user_id` leaves every cook as it is - in a series edit as well, so a meal whose cook was changed on its own keeps it. `repeat_until` and `ingredients` are read with `scope=series` only.

A refusal a user can reach carries a `reason` next to `error` (#1909): `meals_selected_recipe_not_found` (400, the chosen `recipe_id` does not exist).

post.summary: Apply a set of planned meals at once

201.description: Meals created. `data` lists only the meals this call created. `skipped` is present only when `skip_occupied: true` was sent; the status stays 201 even if every assignment was skipped.

index.description: Position of the skipped assignment in `assignments`.

400.description: Missing or invalid assignments, an unknown recipe_id, a `cook_user_id` that is not a household member, `skip_occupied` that is not a boolean, or `skip_occupied` together with `replace_existing`. Nothing is written.

409.description: Idempotency-Key conflict: reused for a different request, or the first attempt is still running

post.description:
Body: { assignments, replace_existing?, skip_occupied? }. Creates one meal per assignment (`date`, `meal_type`, `title`, optional `notes`, `recipe_url`, `recipe_id`, `cook_user_id`, `ingredients`) in a single transaction and returns them. Without `replace_existing` or `skip_occupied`, nothing is skipped or overwritten: the new meals are added next to any meal already planned for the same date and meal type. With `replace_existing: true`, every meal already planned for a date and meal type pair named in `assignments` is deleted first (an occurrence of a weekly series is excepted from the series, so it does not come back); other slots stay untouched. With `skip_occupied: true`, an assignment whose date and meal type pair already holds a meal before the call is not created and is listed in `skipped` instead, with its position in `assignments` as `index`; an occurrence of a weekly series counts as a meal even if its week was never opened, a deleted occurrence does not. Several assignments for the same pair that was empty before the call are all created. `skip_occupied` and `replace_existing` together are refused with 400. If any assignment is invalid or names an unknown recipe, the request is refused with 400 and nothing is written.

A refusal a user can reach carries a `reason` next to `error` (#1909): `meals_selected_recipe_not_found` (400, the chosen `recipe_id` does not exist).

Replaces the recipe including its whole ingredient list - the ingredient rows are deleted and reinserted, so their ids change on every save. Confirmed pantry matches are keyed by the ingredient name and survive that; a match whose ingredient is no longer in the recipe is deleted in the same transaction rather than left behind, so renaming an ingredient really drops its match instead of hiding one that could come back. 409.description: The recipe's ingredients changed since `ingredientIds` were loaded; `recipe` carries the current recipe

post.description:
An open (unchecked) item of the same name on the list - compared trimmed, with whitespace collapsed and case-insensitive - means the ingredient is skipped and counted in `skipped` instead of being added twice; rows of one name in one transfer become one item. This is the one rule of every kitchen path to the shopping list (recipe, meal, meal-plan import, pantry). An optional `quantities` array - one text (or `null`) per ingredient - replaces the stored quantities for this transfer, so a recipe viewed for another number of servings hands over the scaled amounts; names and categories stay the recipe's. With `quantities`, `ingredientIds` is required: the `id` of each ingredient as `GET /recipes` returned it, one per quantity in the same order; a missing or malformed list answers 400. Saving a recipe or syncing it from a provider recreates its ingredient rows, so when the ids no longer match the recipe as it is now, nothing is transferred and the answer is 409 `recipes_ingredients_changed` with the current recipe in `recipe`, instead of putting amounts on the wrong ingredients. Without `quantities` the stored amounts are used and `ingredientIds` is ignored. Creates shopping items, so it requires write access to the `shopping` module in addition to `meals` (which owns `/recipes`) - a credential scoped to the recipes alone is refused with 403.

A refusal a user can reach carries a `reason` next to `error` (#1909): `recipes_recipe_not_found` (404, the recipe does not exist - deleted, or removed by the sync with its recipe provider), `shopping_list_not_found` (404, the chosen shopping list does not exist), `recipes_ingredients_changed` (409, the ingredients changed since `ingredientIds` were loaded; `recipe` carries the current recipe), `cross_module_access` (403, the caller has no write access to the shopping module - for API tokens a `shopping:write` scope).

put.description:
Stores the household's own confirmed match between one ingredient of this recipe and one row of its pantry, or clears it with `pantryItemId: null`. Body: `{ name, pantryItemId }`. Nothing else in Yuvomi ever writes this link - no import, no recipe save, and no name similarity: a guessed identity would be a product catalogue built one inference at a time, which is declined (see #714). The match is keyed by the ingredient name, not by its row id, because saving a recipe replaces all of its ingredient rows. It requires write access to the `pantry` module in addition to `meals` (which owns `/recipes`) - a credential scoped to the recipes alone is refused with 403. 404 when the recipe, the ingredient or the stock row does not exist.

A refusal a user can reach carries a `reason` next to `error` (#1909): `recipes_recipe_not_found` (404, the recipe does not exist - deleted, or removed by the sync with its recipe provider), `recipes_ingredient_not_found` (404, the recipe no longer has this ingredient), `recipes_selected_pantry_item_not_found` (404, the chosen pantry item does not exist), `cross_module_access` (403, the caller has no write access to the pantry module - for API tokens a `pantry:write` scope).

304.description: Unchanged since the given ETag; no request to the provider

400.description: Invalid recipe ID

404.description: Not an imported recipe, or no image at the provider

415.description: The provider returned no image or a type outside PNG, JPEG and WebP

get.description: Proxies the bytes from the recipe provider. A direct to the provider is not possible: its media route wants the same bearer token as every other endpoint, and that token must never reach the client. Same arrangement as the DMS preview proxy. The response carries `Cache-Control: private, no-cache` and an `ETag` derived from the image version, so a client revalidates on every use (through authentication and the module gate) and `If-None-Match` answers `304` without a request to the provider. Errors stay `no-store`.

get.summary: List pantry items with storage locations and categories
get.description: Each pantry item is one batch (a quantity with its own location and best-before date). `product_id` names the household product the batch belongs to: batches with the same name, compared trimmed, case-insensitive and with collapsed whitespace, and the same unit share one product. The server sets it on every write that changes the name, unit or category, and moves the batch to another product when the name or unit no longer matches; a `product_id` in a request body is ignored. Every pantry item response carries it. `products` lists the household products (`id`, `name`, `unit`, `category`, `batch_count`), including products whose last batch is gone (`batch_count` 0).

post.description: Creates or increments pantry items from the checked items of a shopping list. Does not modify the shopping list itself - clear it separately via DELETE /api/v1/shopping/{listId}/items/checked. An item joins an existing batch when the name (trimmed, whitespace collapsed, case-insensitive), the storage location and the unit fit - the same unit, or one that converts (g/kg, ml/l; the amount is converted into the unit of the batch) - and the best-before dates are equal or one of them is empty. Reads the shopping list, so it requires read access to the `shopping` module in addition to `pantry` - a credential without it is refused with 403 and `reason: "cross_module_access"`.

post.description:
Supports optional document-storage attachments via `attachment_name`, `attachment_mime`, `attachment_size`, and `attachment_data` (base64 data URL). New attachments are linked through `attachment_document_id`; legacy events may still return `attachment_data`. Set `target_caldav_account_id` and `target_caldav_calendar_url` to push the event to a CalDAV calendar (omit or null for a local-only event). A new attachment creates a document in the Documents module and therefore needs write access there (member right, for API tokens a `documents:write` scope); without it any non-empty `attachment_data` is refused with 403 before the event is looked up. Replacing or removing an attachment needs read access to the Documents module and sight of the stored document; otherwise the same 403, and the attachment stays. The 403 bodies carry `reason` `ATTACHMENT_UPLOAD_REFUSED` or `ATTACHMENT_CHANGE_REFUSED`. Saving an event carries its visibility and assignees over to the attachment's document only when the save changes who sees the event (its visibility, or the assignees of an event for assignees); a save of the title, time or other fields leaves the document's visibility and shares alone. It opens the document further only for a caller with write access to documents who can see it and may manage it (its creator - for an attachment the event creator - or an admin); otherwise the document keeps the visibility and shares its owner set, so the save neither opens nor narrows it and removes no share. A new attachment uploaded in the same save to an event the caller did not create is only narrowed to the event, never opened further. The default-assignee sync of connected calendars never changes document rights, with one exception: when the event is visible to its assignees and the document is already shared with selected members, the new assignee is added to those shares. Otherwise nothing changes - no document becomes visible to the family, none is opened, narrowed or made private, and no share is removed. A copy made on split or detach belongs to the owner of its source document. A split or a detach copies the attachment for the new series or event only for such a caller; otherwise the new one has no attachment and the original stays on the original series. `start_datetime` and `end_datetime` take the forms of `CalendarDateOrDateTimeInput`: a value without offset is household wall-clock time, a value with `Z` or a numeric offset is read as an instant and converted into the household time zone (`2026-09-21T16:00:00Z` in a Europe/Berlin household is stored as `2026-09-21T18:00`). For an all-day event only the date of such a value counts. Up to v2.68.0 the offset was dropped and its digits kept as wall-clock time. A `recurrence_rule` whose `UNTIL` day lies before the start day is rejected with 400 (`recurrence_rule: the series ends before the start date.`, `reason: calendar_series_ends_before_start`); an `UNTIL` on the start day is a series with one occurrence and is accepted. PUT checks this only when the request changes the rule or the start day, so an imported series that already carries such a rule stays editable; the start day is compared as the household calendar day, so sending the wall-clock form of a stored instant is not a change. For an event with a time zone of its own, whose stored UTC day differs from its local day, only a changed rule is checked, and only an `UNTIL` before both days is rejected. ICS import and calendar sync do not reject it.

A refusal a user can reach carries a `reason` next to `error` (#1909): `calendar_selected_calendar_not_found` (400, the `local_calendar_id` names a local calendar that no longer exists), `calendar_series_no_occurrence` (400, the `recurrence_rule` has no occurrence on or after the start date), `calendar_series_ends_before_start` (400, its `UNTIL` lies before the start day).

put.description:
Creates or updates a linked replacement for one original slot of an eligible local-only series. Scalar fields, assignments, attachments, and `reminder_offsets` are compared with the expanded series defaults. Saving no actual difference restores the normal series occurrence only when a linked replacement existed for that slot; a slot excluded by a deletion or detached replacement remains excluded. A new attachment creates a document in the Documents module and therefore needs write access there (member right, for API tokens a `documents:write` scope); without it any non-empty `attachment_data` is refused with 403 before the event is looked up. Replacing or removing an attachment needs read access to the Documents module and sight of the stored document; otherwise the same 403, and the attachment stays. The 403 bodies carry `reason` `ATTACHMENT_UPLOAD_REFUSED` or `ATTACHMENT_CHANGE_REFUSED`. Saving an event carries its visibility and assignees over to the attachment's document only when the save changes who sees the event (its visibility, or the assignees of an event for assignees); a save of the title, time or other fields leaves the document's visibility and shares alone. It opens the document further only for a caller with write access to documents who can see it and may manage it (its creator - for an attachment the event creator - or an admin); otherwise the document keeps the visibility and shares its owner set, so the save neither opens nor narrows it and removes no share. A new attachment uploaded in the same save to an event the caller did not create is only narrowed to the event, never opened further. The default-assignee sync of connected calendars never changes document rights, with one exception: when the event is visible to its assignees and the document is already shared with selected members, the new assignee is added to those shares. Otherwise nothing changes - no document becomes visible to the family, none is opened, narrowed or made private, and no share is removed. A copy made on split or detach belongs to the owner of its source document. A split or a detach copies the attachment for the new series or event only for such a caller; otherwise the new one has no attachment and the original stays on the original series.

A refusal a user can reach carries a `reason` next to `error` (#1909): `not_owner` (403, without the module's `*_edit_others` capability only events you created or are assigned to can be changed or deleted - R23), `calendar_series_not_found` (404, the series does not exist or is not visible to the caller).

The former date-only form `YYYY-MM-DD` is still accepted for a timed series with its earlier meaning; when it matches two occurrences (the night of a clock change) the answer is 409 with reason `ambiguous_recurrence_id`.

put.description:
Supports document-storage attachments. Omit attachment fields to preserve the current attachment, send new `attachment_data` to create and link a document, or set `remove_attachment` to true to unlink it without deleting the library document. Legacy events may still return `attachment_data`. A recurrence-rule or anchor change that would orphan linked replacements returns 409 with `calendar_override_orphans` and the exact `orphaned_override_count`; retry with the same value in `confirmed_orphan_count` to preserve those replacements as standalone events. The same confirmation is required before assigning an outbound target to a series with linked replacements. Changing a mirrored field (title, description, location, color, all-day, start/end, recurrence) of an event synced to Google pushes the change there, and switching `target_google_calendar_id` moves it to the other Google calendar. The remote call runs after the response and is retried by the next sync run if it fails. PUT stores the validated start and end, exactly as POST does; up to v2.68.0 it wrote the raw request value. `start_datetime` may be omitted to keep it, but an empty or null start is rejected with 400; an empty or null `end_datetime` clears the end. A new attachment creates a document in the Documents module and therefore needs write access there (member right, for API tokens a `documents:write` scope); without it any non-empty `attachment_data` is refused with 403 before the event is looked up. Replacing or removing an attachment needs read access to the Documents module and sight of the stored document; otherwise the same 403, and the attachment stays. The 403 bodies carry `reason` `ATTACHMENT_UPLOAD_REFUSED` or `ATTACHMENT_CHANGE_REFUSED`. Saving an event carries its visibility and assignees over to the attachment's document only when the save changes who sees the event (its visibility, or the assignees of an event for assignees); a save of the title, time or other fields leaves the document's visibility and shares alone. It opens the document further only for a caller with write access to documents who can see it and may manage it (its creator - for an attachment the event creator - or an admin); otherwise the document keeps the visibility and shares its owner set, so the save neither opens nor narrows it and removes no share. A new attachment uploaded in the same save to an event the caller did not create is only narrowed to the event, never opened further. The default-assignee sync of connected calendars never changes document rights, with one exception: when the event is visible to its assignees and the document is already shared with selected members, the new assignee is added to those shares. Otherwise nothing changes - no document becomes visible to the family, none is opened, narrowed or made private, and no share is removed. A copy made on split or detach belongs to the owner of its source document. A split or a detach copies the attachment for the new series or event only for such a caller; otherwise the new one has no attachment and the original stays on the original series. `start_datetime` and `end_datetime` take the forms of `CalendarDateOrDateTimeInput`: a value without offset is household wall-clock time, a value with `Z` or a numeric offset is read as an instant and converted into the household time zone (`2026-09-21T16:00:00Z` in a Europe/Berlin household is stored as `2026-09-21T18:00`). For an all-day event only the date of such a value counts. Up to v2.68.0 the offset was dropped and its digits kept as wall-clock time. A `recurrence_rule` whose `UNTIL` day lies before the start day is rejected with 400 (`recurrence_rule: the series ends before the start date.`, `reason: calendar_series_ends_before_start`); an `UNTIL` on the start day is a series with one occurrence and is accepted. PUT checks this only when the request changes the rule or the start day, so an imported series that already carries such a rule stays editable; the start day is compared as the household calendar day, so sending the wall-clock form of a stored instant is not a change. For an event with a time zone of its own, whose stored UTC day differs from its local day, only a changed rule is checked, and only an `UNTIL` before both days is rejected. ICS import and calendar sync do not reject it.

A refusal a user can reach carries a `reason` next to `error` (#1909): `not_owner` (403, without the module's `*_edit_others` capability only events you created or are assigned to can be changed or deleted - R23), `calendar_event_not_found` (404, the event does not exist or is not visible to the caller), `calendar_selected_calendar_not_found` (400, the `local_calendar_id` names a local calendar that no longer exists), `calendar_series_no_occurrence` (400, the `recurrence_rule` has no occurrence on or after the start date), `calendar_series_ends_before_start` (400, its `UNTIL` lies before the start day).

get.summary: Count imported events a default-assignee backfill would fill
get.description:
Query: `moved_after` (optional) - the `moved_next` of the previous page. Response: { data: { count, token, moved, moved_total, moved_offset, moved_next } }. `count` counts already imported events from calendars of every account that carry a default assignee and are not assigned to anyone yet (#1154). `token` fingerprints exactly that set - which events, and which person each would get - and is meant to be sent back as `expected_token` (#1171). `moved` lists, one entry per event, events whose assignees are still exactly the untouched default assignees of another calendar of the same account (same provider; for CalDAV the same account), in a calendar with different default assignees, never edited in Yuvomi and not pushed out (#1307): { event_id, title, start_datetime, all_day, calendar_name, from_user_ids, from_names, to_user_ids, to_names, from_user_id, from_name, to_user_id, to_name } - the single fields carry the first person and all names joined (#1897). Only events the requesting admin may see under the calendar visibility rule are listed, counted or changed (no admin bypass, as everywhere in the calendar); `count` and `token` only count and name no event, as before. The list comes in pages of at most 5000 entries, oldest start first: `moved_total` counts all, `moved_offset` those before this page, and `moved_next` is the cursor for the next page (null on the last), so a page left entirely unticked does not hide the ones after it. Such an event may have been moved between calendars before the move started carrying the assignment along, or it may sit in a calendar whose default assignee was changed later; the data cannot tell the two apart, so these events are not part of `count` and change only when picked one by one.

Admin-only endpoint.

post.summary: Apply default assignees to already imported events

409.description: Idempotency-Key conflict: reused for a different request, or the first attempt is still running

post.description:
Body: { expected_count, expected_token?, moves? } - the count and the token the confirmation was based on; when the candidate set changed since, the call answers 409 with { data: { count, token, moved, moved_total, moved_offset, moved_next } } (the first page) and changes nothing. With `expected_token` a change of the same size is caught as well (an event assigned by hand while a new import takes its place, or a calendar switched to another person); without it only the count is compared (#1171). `moves` is the list of `moved` entries the admin picked, each as { event_id, from_user_ids, to_user_ids } exactly as listed (the earlier form { event_id, from_user_id, to_user_id } still works for one person), each event at most once and at most 5000 entries, as many as the preview lists; a longer list answers 400 with a message naming the limit (#1307); each entry is checked on its own against the same rule and visibility as the preview, without loading the list and without needing a page, and an entry that does not match that way also answers 409. Without `moves` no existing assignment is changed. Only the confirmed candidate list and the picked moves are processed, each event re-checked when written, so `assigned` can be lower than expected if events changed in the meantime. Response: { data: { assigned } }. Runs in batches so a long history does not block other requests; inherited reminders whose time has passed are marked dismissed. A default assignee only reaches events imported after it was set. This one-off action assigns it to the events already imported from that calendar, across all accounts, but only where an event is not assigned to anyone yet: an assignment made by hand is left alone (#1154). It cannot tell a never-assigned event from one whose assignment was removed by hand. ICS subscriptions are not included.

Admin-only endpoint.

put.description:
On a contact linked to an account (`family_user_id`), `email` and `emails` can only be changed by that member or an admin, in a session or with an unscoped token; anyone else, and any token scoped to modules, is refused with 403. Addresses are compared without regard to letter case; sending them unchanged or only in another case is not a change, and the stored spelling is kept. When the member edits their own linked contact, a newly added address that already belongs to another account (split-expense guests excluded) is refused with 409 and `reason: "email_in_use"`; an admin may assign it. All other fields stay editable for anyone with write access to contacts. `birthday_year_unknown` (boolean or 0/1) marks a birthday without a year (#2095): `birthday` then carries the placeholder year 2000 whatever year is sent, and responses carry the flag as 0 or 1. Omitted, the stored flag stays; turning it off needs a `birthday` with its real year in the same request.

get.description: Each loan carries `due_day` (1 to 31, or `null`), `next_due_month` (`YYYY-MM`) and `next_due_date` (`YYYY-MM-DD`): the due day in the month the next installment is due, clamped to the last day of a shorter month. For a loan without a due day, `next_due_date` is the 1st of `next_due_month` when that month lies before the household's current month (a booking date, not a due date), and `null` for an installment due in the current or a later month. Both are `null` once the loan is settled. `projected_end_month` (`YYYY-MM`) is the month of the last installment: the remaining installments counted from the later of `next_due_month` and the household's current month, following the payments actually booked for a loan with interest; `null` once settled and for a loan whose installment does not cover its interest. A loan with interest carries `interest.current_rate`, the rate that applies today: that of the installment due in the household's current month, at least the next unrecorded one (the fixed rate during the fixed-rate period, the follow-up rate after it). `summary.by_direction.borrowed` and `summary.by_direction.lent` carry the summary figures per direction (`count`, `active_count`, `has_interest`, `total_amount`, `paid_amount`, `remaining_amount`, `remaining_principal`, `remaining_installments`): a borrowed balance is owed by the household, a lent one is owed to it. The top-level figures add both directions.

get.description: Each entry carries `attachments`. Linked documents follow the Documents module: a document the caller cannot see is left out, and without access to the Documents module (for API tokens a `documents:read` scope) `attachments` is `null` - neither the documents nor their number are told, and a record with receipts looks the same as one without. With `month`, the list also carries the subscription payments that follow a subscription's booked entry, worked out from its cycle when the month is read and not stored: `expected: true`, `id: null`, `subscription_id`, `is_pending: 1`. They are in no total, cannot be changed, confirmed or deleted through this API, and are left out with `loan_id`, `account_id` and `q`. Months before the household's current month carry none. In personal budget mode they reach only a viewer who sees both the booked entry with its purpose and the subscription; they are never returned masked. `meta.expected_omitted: true` appears only when the projection hit its limit of 5000 lines; the list then carries none.

parameters.description: View filter when the household runs in personal budget mode (preference `budget_mode=personal`): `mine` shows entries you own, `household` shows the shared pot. Ignored in shared mode. Entries also carry `owner_id` and `visibility` (`private`|`shared`|`shared_amount`); private entries are only visible to their owner (no admin bypass), and on a `shared_amount` entry of someone else only amount, date and account remain (`details_hidden: true`). Each entry carries `attachments`: linked documents from the documents module, filtered by document visibility.

parameters.name: category
parameters.description: Only entries of this category key; an unknown key is ignored. The filter sees the same view as the response: in personal budget mode an entry of someone else whose details are hidden from you (`shared_amount`) carries the category `__private__` and matches only that key, like the catch-all bucket in the summary and statistics.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Search the ledger instead of listing one month: matches the entry title across all months, inside words, ignoring case and accents (`muller` finds `Müller`). `month` and `category` are ignored; `account_id` and `scope` still apply. delete.description:
Deletes the folder and all subfolders. `documents=unfile` keeps every document row and clears its folder link, including documents hidden from the caller, while reporting only the visible unfile count. `documents=delete` requires the opaque HMAC snapshot from the latest delete-impact response; the token binds exact folder identities and the document and collateral-link identities visible to the caller. The route then sequentially deletes visible document content and rows while locking the previewed identities, subtree targets and new document links. Documents hidden from the caller are never deleted, locked or reported in either mode: they keep their row and lose only their folder link, as with `documents=unfile`, so the answer is the same with and without them. Destructive deletion is rejected before the first storage operation: first with 409 `FOLDER_CONTENT_CHANGED` if the previewed visible identities changed, then with 403 `FOLDER_DOCUMENTS_NOT_MANAGEABLE` if a non-admin does not own every visible document. `documents=unfile` is not blocked by a single-document deletion in progress, only by an overlapping folder deletion. A 207 response distinguishes storage, database-row and concurrent-content failures while retaining the folder subtree; it names only documents visible to the caller.

A refusal a user can reach carries a `reason` next to `error` (#1909): `documents_folder_not_found` (404, the folder does not exist).

get.description: Household preferences. Language fields: `language` (explicitly chosen data language, or `null` for automatic), plus two read-only values — `language_effective` (what actually applies: `language`, else the language part of `region`, else `en`) and `language_auto` (what automatic mode alone would yield, ignoring `language`). The data language decides in which language the server *stores* content it generates itself - birthday event titles, loan instalments, and the public/school holiday names pulled from OpenHolidays (#946) - so that the API, the ICS feed and calendar sync all agree. Changing it re-syncs the holiday cache on the next run, because that cache holds translated names rather than keys. Weather fields: `weather_provider` (`open-meteo` | `openweathermap` | `null` = auto-detect from env), `weather_lat`, `weather_lon`, `weather_city`, `weather_units` (`metric` | `imperial`). `weather_source` (read-only) says which household weather configuration applies: `{ source, provider, lat, lon, city, units }` where `source` is `db` (stored here), `env` (`WEATHER_*` or legacy `OPENWEATHER_*` server environment) or `none`. A stored configuration always wins over the environment; the per-member location is not part of it. It never contains an API key. Holiday fields: `holiday_country` (ISO-3166 alpha-2 or `null`), `holiday_subdivision` (e.g. `DE-BY` or `null`), `holiday_group` (school-holiday group for multilingual cantons, e.g. `CH-BE-VS`, or `null`), `holiday_show_public`, `holiday_show_school` (booleans), `holiday_public_color`, `holiday_school_color` (hex), `holiday_last_sync`. Overview fields: `dashboard_widgets` (the tile arrangement that applies to the calling user) and `dashboard_today_glance` (header band on/off), plus `dashboard_widgets_default` / `dashboard_today_glance_default` (what the household published as its default, `dashboard_widgets_default` is `null` when nothing was published) and `dashboard_follows_default` (`true` when the caller has no arrangement of their own and therefore follows the household).

put.description: `language` is admin-only: an ISO-639-1 code with a locale file, or `null`/`""` to fall back to automatic derivation from `region`. Changing it (or `region`, or `date_format`) re-titles the stored birthday events so every channel stays consistent. `timezone` is admin-only too: an IANA zone (validated against ICU, so aliases like `Europe/Kiev` are accepted), or `null`/`""` to fall back to the `TZ` env var, then the host zone, then UTC. It is the household zone used wherever a time carries none of its own - the calendar day server-side jobs call "today", the zone of the exported ICS feed, and the clock time events arrive with in Google and Outlook. The GET response carries both views: `timezone` (what is chosen, `null` for automatic) and `timezone_effective` (what applies, never `null`). `timezone_hint_dismissed` (admin-only boolean, household-wide) records that an admin has answered the question whether the household should adopt the browser zone; every accepted `timezone` write sets it to `true` as well. Weather fields (`weather_provider`, `weather_lat`, `weather_lon`, `weather_city`, `weather_units`) and holiday fields (`holiday_country`, `holiday_subdivision`, `holiday_group`, `holiday_show_public`, `holiday_show_school`, `holiday_public_color`, `holiday_school_color`) are admin-only. `weather_lat`/`weather_lon` are validated to ±90 / ±180, and `null` deletes them; colors must be 6-digit hex. Module feature toggles `health_cycle_enabled` (show the health cycle tab household-wide) and `rewards_require_approval` (redemptions need admin approval) are admin-only booleans, both default `true`. `health_cycle_enabled_user` is the per-user opt-out for the same tab and is writable by anyone for themselves; it can only narrow the household setting, never widen it. The GET response exposes all three views: `health_cycle_enabled` (household), `health_cycle_enabled_user` (mine) and the read-only `health_cycle_effective` (both combined, which is what the UI renders). Overview fields: `dashboard_widgets` (array of `{id, visible, order, size, options?}`; `options` is stored but not interpreted - the server validates only its shape: a flat object, at most 8 keys, values boolean, finite number, short string or list of short strings) and `dashboard_today_glance` are personal and writable by anyone for themselves; sending `null` for either deletes the personal value, so the caller follows the household default again - including every later change to it. `dashboard_widgets_default` and `dashboard_today_glance_default` are the household default and admin-only; they never overwrite a member who has an arrangement of their own, and `null` removes the default.

get.description:
The caller's own reminders that are not due yet, for a client that schedules them on the device. Both edges of the window count, and it spans at most 14 days. Only what lies after the current moment comes back, also when `from` is in the past: a reminder is in `GET /reminders/pending` from the moment it is due and in this list until then, never in both. Sorted by the moment the reminder fires, at most 200 rows, counted after everything the caller may not see is left out. The list is a snapshot: the server keeps rebuilding derived types, and it does not know what a client scheduled.

The rules of `GET /reminders/pending` apply: own, non-dismissed rows only, nothing whose entity is hidden from the caller, no task or event that is gone, nothing from a module the household switched off, and only origins the caller may read. On top of them, a task that is done or archived is left out, and comes back when it is reopened: what a client schedules fires without asking again. A client still has to cancel its own notification when a task is checked off, because this list only changes at the next fetch. An API token needs `calendar:read` to reach this route and a read scope of the module behind each origin for its rows, for example `tasks:read` for `task`; a row the caller may not read is left out, not refused.

Use `fires_at`, not `remind_at`, to schedule: `remind_at` is UTC without a suffix, and rows written up to v2.68.0 may carry an offset.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Start of the window, included. Without `Z` or an offset the value is UTC, as in `remind_at`; a date alone is midnight UTC; fractions of a second are dropped. Percent-encode a `+` in an offset (`%2B`): unencoded it reads as a space and answers 400.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: End of the window, included. At most 14 days after `from`. Without `Z` or an offset the value is UTC, as in `remind_at`; a date alone is midnight UTC; fractions of a second are dropped. Percent-encode a `+` in an offset (`%2B`): unencoded it reads as a space and answers 400.

parameters.name: types
parameters.description: Comma-separated origins to keep, for example `task,event`. It only narrows: an origin the caller may not read stays out, and an unknown value answers 400. Without it, every origin the caller may read comes back.

post.description:
`pantry_item` is rejected with 400: the notification run rebuilds pantry reminders every pass, so a hand-set date would be gone within a minute. Reading and dismissing work as for any other reminder. Other derived types (subscription, inventory) stay settable - there the module only writes when its object changes. The entity has to exist and be visible to the caller under the rule of its own module (task and event visibility, shared calendar subscriptions, private subscriptions in personal budget mode); otherwise the answer is 404, the same for both cases. `GET /reminders/pending` and notifications skip a reminder whose entity is hidden from its recipient; the reminder is kept and resumes once the entity is visible again. `remind_at` is stored as UTC without a zone suffix, always as `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS`. A value without offset already is UTC and is only brought into that form: missing seconds become `:00`, fractions are dropped, and a date alone becomes midnight UTC, the moment it fired at before. A value with `Z` or a numeric offset is read as an instant and converted: `2026-09-22T18:00:00+02:00` is stored as `2026-09-22T16:00:00`. Up to v2.68.0 values were stored as sent; rows with an offset from then are still read as the instant they name and fire on time. For `entity_type=event`, a reminder set by the person who CREATED the event is also written for everyone assigned to it, as a row of their own - so it reaches them by push and shows up when they open the event, instead of leaving them an empty field that reads as "none set". A reminder an assignee set for themselves is never overwritten by this, a dismissed one is not resurrected unless the time actually changed, and removing the assignment removes the inherited row. Anyone other than the creator sets reminders for themselves only.

A refusal a user can reach carries a `reason` next to `error` (#1909): `module_access_denied` (403, the caller may not write to the module the reminder's entity belongs to - for an API token the `<module>:write` scope of that module, e.g. `calendar:write` for `entity_type=event`).

A hit whose words are not all in its `title` carries `excerpt`: a short piece of the first visible field that holds a missing word (description, note text, notes), cut at word boundaries with `…` where it was shortened. A recurring event in `events` carries the `start_datetime` of its next occurrence from today (household time zone, looking two years ahead), as `GET /api/v1/calendar/search` does; `id` stays the id of the series. A series without an upcoming occurrence keeps the start of its first one. Up to v2.71.0 the series start was returned. A hit in `birthdays` carries `year_unknown` (boolean): only day and month of its `birth_date` are known (#2095).

post.description:
Takes a `user_id`, or a `contact_id` that is turned into a guest user when the contact has none yet. A `contact_id` needs read access to the Contacts module (for API tokens `contacts:read`); without it, and for an unknown contact, the answer is the same 404 and nothing is created. A contact without an account is linked to the new guest and needs write access to Contacts (`contacts:write`); without it the answer is 403 and nothing is written. If that contact carries an address that already belongs to another account (split-expense guests excluded), a caller who is not an admin gets 409 with `reason: "email_in_use"` and nothing is created. While the group is archived this is refused with `409` and `reason: "group_archived"` (checked after `404` and `403`); restore the group first.

A refusal a user can reach carries a `reason` next to `error` (#1909): `cross_module_access` (403, adding a person without an account creates a contact and needs write access to contacts - for API tokens a `contacts:write` scope).

get.description: Active expenses, newest first: `expense_date`, then `created_at`, then `id`, each descending - expenses written in the same second keep a fixed order. Page through every expense with the cursor: pass `before_date`, `before_at` and `before_id` from `pagination.next_cursor` of the previous page; an expense added or deleted meanwhile shifts nothing. Without a cursor the endpoint behaves as before (`limit`, `offset`). `pagination.has_more` is exact: false when the page holds the last expense, also when exactly `limit` remain; `pagination.next_cursor` is null then. A partial cursor, or a cursor together with a non-zero `offset`, answers 400. Each expense carries `attachments`. Linked documents follow the Documents module: a document the caller cannot see is left out, and without access to the Documents module (for API tokens a `documents:read` scope) `attachments` is `null` - neither the documents nor their number are told, and a record with receipts looks the same as one without.

get.description: Active ones first, then by `next_run_date`. Besides its columns every recurring expense carries: `payer_name`; `participants` and `splits`, the stored split as input (what `split_snapshot` holds; a legacy snapshot that is a list of finished shares gives its people as `participants`); `blocked_reason`, why the hourly run would pause it on its next date (`split_invalid`: the stored split cannot be booked, `not_a_member`: the payer or a participant is no longer a member of the group) or null, measured against the current state with the run's own check; `can_edit`, whether the caller may update, delete, pause and resume it (group owner/admin or whoever created it); `failed_at`, when the hourly run first failed to book it for an unexpected reason (an ISO timestamp, or null): such a recurring expense is not paused and is retried every hour; a booking, an update or a pause for a known reason clears it; and, on a paused one, `missed_count` and `resume_date`: how many dates a resume without `missed: "book"` skips and the date it lands on (0 and null while it is active). Every recurring expense carries `anchor_day`, the day of the month it is meant for (1-31), taken from the first `next_run_date` when it is created and again whenever an update changes `next_run_date` or `frequency`; it cannot be set directly. Monthly and yearly steps clamp to the last day of a shorter month and return to the anchor where the month has it: a series on the 31st books on 28 or 29 February and on 31 March, a yearly one from 29 February books on 28 February and on 29 February again in a leap year. Weekly series step by seven days.

Anything else is answered with `400` and nothing is stored. Without `missed` the date is kept, as before this option existed. "Today" is the day in the household time zone; a date that is today is not missed. On an update `missed` only applies when the call changes `next_run_date`. Anything other than `skip` or `book` is refused with 400 and `reason: "invalid_missed"`, and nothing is stored. put.description: Allowed for group owners/admins and for whoever created it. A partial update: every field the call omits stays as it is - title, amount, currency, payer, category, description, rhythm, date, split method, participants and `splits`. Send `description` as `null` or `""` to clear it. The resulting recurring expense as a whole runs through the same check as creating one, and a refused update changes nothing: changing only the amount of an `exact` split is answered with `400` because the stored shares no longer add up. Amounts are decimal strings with a dot (`"12.50"`, not a number), with at most the currency's decimal places, and must be greater than zero: `0`, `-0` and negative values are answered with `400`. `budget_category` is a key from `GET /api/v1/budget/categories` of type `expense`, or `null` for none; an unknown key answers 400. On an update an omitted `budget_category` stays as it is, and so does the key the row already carries even when that category no longer exists. A budget category that split expenses or series still use cannot be deleted. `category` is the older split-expense category and is kept as it was. With `split_method: "exact"`, every participant needs a `splits[].amount` under the same rule, and the shares must add up to the expense amount. The split is checked when the recurring expense is created, by the same rule as a single expense: `payer_id` and every entry of `participants` must be members of the group, `exact` amounts must add up to the amount, `percentage` values to 100, and `shares` must be positive integers. Anything else is answered with `400` and nothing is stored. Without `currency` an `amount` is read in the currency of the recurring expense. A date that was already booked cannot be triggered again: a `next_run_date` that differs from the stored one must lie after the last date booked from this recurring expense (the latest `expense_date` of its expenses, deleted ones included); otherwise the answer is `400` with `reason: "next_run_not_after_last_booking"` and `last_booked`. Clients that show an edit form should send only the fields the user changed, so a form opened before the last run does not send its old date back. Expenses already booked keep their values; the next date is booked with the new ones. `anchor_day` follows `next_run_date` only when the call changes the date or the frequency, so saving a series from the 31st while it stands on 28 February leaves it on the 31st. A `next_run_date` before today can be answered with `missed` (#1748), the same choice a resume takes: `skip` stores the first date of the series that is not before today, counted from the given date in whole intervals exactly as the hourly run counts (with the `anchor_day` of the given date), so nothing is booked for the past; `book` keeps the date, and the hourly run then books every missed date, one per run, each with its original date. Without `missed` the date is kept, as before this option existed. "Today" is the day in the household time zone; a date that is today is not missed. On an update `missed` only applies when the call changes `next_run_date`. Anything other than `skip` or `book` is refused with 400 and `reason: "invalid_missed"`, and nothing is stored. `paused_at` is not touched: a paused recurring expense stays paused until it is resumed. Writes a `recurring_edited` activity entry with title and amount. The response has the shape of the list. While the group is archived this is refused with `409` and `reason: "group_archived"` (checked after `404` and `403`); restore the group first.

post.description: A toggle: an active recurring expense is paused, a paused one is resumed. Allowed for group owners/admins and for whoever created it. Resuming skips the dates that fell due during the pause: `next_run_date` moves to the first date of the series that is not before today, counted from the old `next_run_date` in whole intervals exactly as the hourly run counts (with the same `anchor_day`, so a series on the 31st resumes on the 31st or the last day of the month), and nothing is booked for the past. "Today" is the day in the household time zone; a date that is today is not missed and is booked by the next run. A resume that skipped dates writes `metadata.skipped` (their number) into its `recurring_resumed` activity entry. Send `missed: "book"` to keep `next_run_date` instead: the hourly run then books every missed date, one per run, each with its original date (the behaviour before this option existed). When the call pauses, `missed` changes nothing about the pause, but its value is checked on every call: anything other than `skip` or `book` is refused with 400 and the recurring expense stays as it was. While the group is archived this is refused with `409` and `reason: "group_archived"` (checked after `404` and `403`); restore the group first.

post.description:
The household day decides `today_session` and the date of the calendar entry and payment task of a check-in. With a household time zone set, that zone decides and client values are ignored. Otherwise the optional `timezone` (IANA name, query or body) the client displays in decides, then the time zone of the server. A caller without `housekeeping_view_amounts` writes no amounts: a check-in takes the rate from the profile, check-out keeps the extras, an update keeps rate, extras and minutes, and payment task texts fall back to the household language. Paying and taking back a payment are refused with 403 and `reason: amounts_hidden`.
