get.description: Returns discovered third-party modules from the modules directory, including normalized capabilities (widgets, permissions, API prefix) when declared in module.json. Pass `admin=1` as an admin to include disabled and errored modules and the `install` metadata (source, URL, commit, whether it was approved, who installed it); other listings leave `install` out.

Whether installing from Settings is switched on by the operator (`webInstall`, `MODULES_ALLOW_WEB_INSTALL`), whether the modules folder on the server is writable (it is not on read-only mounts), whether it survives an update (`persistent`: false in a container without a volume on the modules folder, null when unknown) and the archive size limit. When `webInstall` or `writable` is false the install routes refuse (403 or 503) and modules can only be copied in by hand. The Settings page treats `persistent: false` the same way and shows the manual way, although the routes themselves still answer there.

Admin-only endpoint.

post.summary: Install an extension module from a ZIP archive

201.description: Module installed (or replaced). `data` is the module as listed by GET /api/v1/modules?admin=1.

400.description: Invalid archive or manifest. `reason` is one of `bad_url`, `not_zip`, `unsafe_path`, `symlink`, `encrypted`, `zip64`, `method`, `crc`, `duplicate`, `corrupt` (also for an incomplete upload), `bad_manifest`, `no_manifest`, `path_not_found`.

403.description: Not an admin, installing from Settings switched off on this server (`module_web_install_disabled`), or not a browser session (`module_session_required`)

409.description: A module with this id is installed (`exists`, with `existing: { id, name, version, install }` and `incoming: { id, name, version }`; `existing.install` is always the install record, because only a recorded module reaches this answer; retry with overwrite, which leaves the module disabled until it is approved again), the folder `modules/<id>` carries no install record, so it was copied to the server by hand and is not replaced from here (`not_web_installed`, without `existing`, with or without overwrite; remove the folder on the server first, then install again), `modules/<id>` is a symbolic link or a file (`not_a_module`, cannot be replaced from here), or another install/delete is running (`busy`).

413.description: Archive larger than 20 MB (`too_large`), too many entries (`too_many_entries`) or suspicious compression (`bomb`).

422.description: The archive holds several modules (`multiple`, with `candidates: [{ path, id, name, version }]`), or `path` names a folder that holds several; retry with `path` set to one candidate (`""` is the archive root).

429.description: Install rate limit reached (`install_rate_limited`): 10 installs or 30 attempts in 10 minutes

503.description: The modules folder on the server is not writable (`not_writable`).

post.description:
Exists only where the operator set `MODULES_ALLOW_WEB_INSTALL=true` (off by default): otherwise 403 `module_web_install_disabled`, before the body is read. A module is same-origin JavaScript that runs with the session of every member who opens it; installing one is equivalent to copying its folder onto the server. Every install and every replace lands DISABLED: the install record in the module folder (`install.approved: false`) keeps it off, whatever the database says, until an admin enables it with PATCH /api/v1/modules/{id} from a browser session. A replace resets that approval even when it comes from the same repository. Only the module folder is copied, files other than web assets are skipped and listed in `skipped`, and nothing from the archive runs on the server. Limited to 10 install requests per 10 minutes per user; the 409 `exists` and 422 `multiple` answers that ask back do not count there, but every request counts against a second limit of 30 attempts per 10 minutes, because those answers come after the download and the unpack. Errors carry a stable `reason`. Only from a signed-in browser session: an API token (and therefore the MCP bridge) gets 403 `module_session_required`, and the operation is not offered as an MCP tool. The request body is the raw ZIP file, up to 20 MB.

Admin-only endpoint.

parameters.description: Set to `1` to replace an installed module with the same id (after a 409 `exists`). Only a module that carries an install record is replaced; a folder copied to the server by hand answers 409 `not_web_installed` with or without this flag.

parameters.description: Folder inside the archive that holds module.json, relative to the single top folder if there is one (after a 422 `multiple`). Present but empty (`path=`) selects the archive root.

Every install and every replace lands DISABLED: the install record in the module folder (`install.approved: false`) keeps it off, whatever the database says, until an admin enables it with PATCH /api/v1/modules/{id} from a browser session. A replace resets that approval even when it comes from the same repository. Only the module folder is copied, files other than web assets are skipped and listed in `skipped`, and nothing from the archive runs on the server. Limited to 10 install requests per 10 minutes per user; the 409 `exists` and 422 `multiple` answers that ask back do not count there, but every request counts against a second limit of 30 attempts per 10 minutes, because those answers come after the download and the unpack. Errors carry a stable `reason`. Only from a signed-in browser session: an API token (and therefore the MCP bridge) gets 403 `module_session_required`, and the operation is not offered as an MCP tool. Accepted URLs: `https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>` (also without `https://`), `.../tree/<ref>[/<path>]`, `.../releases/tag/<tag>`, `.../releases/latest` and bare `<owner>/<repo>`. If the URL names no tag or branch, the latest release is used, or the default branch when there is no release. A tree URL that points at a folder holding several modules answers 422 `multiple`. The archive is downloaded only from api.github.com, github.com and codeload.github.com.

patch.description:
Enabling (`enabled: true`) is the admin's approval of installed code and is only possible from a signed-in browser session: an API token, and therefore the MCP bridge, gets 403 `module_session_required`. For a module installed from Settings it also writes `approved: true` into the install record in the module folder, so the approval survives a restored or fresh database. That write runs under the install lock: while an install or delete is running (a GitHub download can take up to 30 s) enabling answers 409 `busy`, and when the module folder is not writable for the server it answers 503 `not_writable`. Error bodies carry `reason` where one is known. Disabling (`enabled: false`) works with a token as well; it sets the household switch and then writes `approved: false` back into the install record (best effort: a read-only folder does not stop it, and while an install or delete holds the lock the record is left as it is, since disabling never waits), so `approved` always means that an admin has this version switched on. The operation stays available to MCP for that direction.

post.description:
Body: { scheduled_at?, schedule_id?, status?, taken_at?, dose_qty?, note?, stock_deduct? }; `status` defaults to `pending`. Only a `taken` entry keeps `taken_at`: sent alongside `pending` or `skipped`, it is dropped and stored as null. `stock_deduct` (not negative) lowers the recorded stock in the same transaction as the log entry, never below 0, and only for a `taken` entry; a medication without recorded stock keeps none (#2069). One entry per planned occurrence: when an entry for the same `schedule_id` and `scheduled_at` exists, it is updated and the answer is `200`, and stock is deducted only when it turns `taken`. Send an `Idempotency-Key` to retry an as-needed dose safely. The answer carries `stock_deducted`: what actually came off the stock (0 without recorded stock, less than asked when the stock ran out) - the amount `POST /logs/{id}/undo` credits back. A dose that ends up `taken` without a `taken_at` gets the current minute in household wall-clock time, so no path stores `taken` without a time. get.description: Scoped to the viewer; `?user_id=`, `from`, `to` filters supported. Each row also carries `feelings` (array of mood keys, from the normalized `cycle_day_log_feelings` table); the legacy scalar `mood` is still returned for backward compatibility; it is only written (set to NULL) when a save's body includes `feelings` or `mood` as a key, and left untouched otherwise. `cervix_mucus`, `lh_test`, `pregnancy_test` and `intimacy` (all nullable enums, see the POST body) are included ONLY when the caller is the row's own owner - stripped from every other read regardless of the row's `visibility`, since sharing a day does not imply sharing fertility-test results or a sex-life entry.

post.summary: Upsert a cycle day log (one per person and day)

409.description: Idempotency-Key conflict: reused for a different request, or the first attempt is still running

post.description: Body: { log_date, flow?, note?, visibility?, symptoms?, basal_temp?, basal_temp_unit?, cervix_mucus?, lh_test?, pregnancy_test?, intimacy?, feelings? }. `cervix_mucus` ∈ dry/sticky/creamy/watery/eggwhite; `lh_test`/`pregnancy_test` ∈ negative/positive; `intimacy` ∈ protected/unprotected/solo. `feelings` is an array from a fixed 7-key set (great/good/neutral/sensitive/sad/irritable/anxious, same as the frontend's MOOD_TYPES) - any other value is a 400, not stored as free text. The legacy single-value `mood` is still accepted and validated against the same fixed set, treated as `feelings: [mood]` when `feelings` is absent. A save whose body includes either `feelings` or `mood` as a key fully replaces the stored feelings rows (delete + re-insert) and sets the `mood` column to NULL; a save that includes neither key leaves both the existing feelings rows and the `mood` column untouched, so an unrelated field change cannot silently clear a frozen legacy mood value. This is NOT the same as `symptoms`: `symptoms` is fully replaced on every save (an omitted `symptoms` array normalizes to empty and clears any existing rows), while `feelings`/`mood` are only replaced when the request actually names one of those two keys.

post.description: Body: { csv: string }. Header-tolerant CSV in the export's own column order (`start_date`, `end_date` first - see GET /export/cycle); extra columns are ignored. Accepts both comma and semicolon separators (German Excel exports use `;`) and both `YYYY-MM-DD` and `DD.MM.YYYY` dates (again a German-export accommodation). All-or-nothing: any invalid row rejects the whole import with 400 and up to the first 10 row errors, nothing is inserted. A row whose `start_date` matches an existing period of the caller is skipped (counted, not an error); other overlaps are allowed. Rejects with 400 if the payload exceeds 100 KB or 500 data rows. New periods take the caller's `default_visibility` from `/cycle/settings` (falls back to `private`). Response: `{ imported, skipped, errors: [] }`. Re-syncs the caller's cycle reminders once after commit. A refusal a user reaches with the file carries a `reason` (#1909): `health_cycle_import_too_large` with `params.limit_kb`, `health_cycle_import_no_rows` (header only), `health_cycle_import_too_many_rows` with `params.limit`.

patch.description:
Only the fields present are changed. Sending a nutrient as null clears it back to "not stated"; sending 0 states zero. Timestamps (`measured_at`, `performed_at`, `consumed_at`, `scheduled_at`, `taken_at`) are household wall-clock time, stored as `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM`. A value without offset is taken as such; a value with `Z` or a numeric offset is read as an instant and converted into the household time zone, so the same moment sent in UTC or with a local offset lands on the same minute. Up to v2.68.0 the offset was dropped and its digits kept.

Admin-only endpoint.

post.description:
Calls the configured Immich server once and reports how many photos the album holds. Answers 502 if Immich cannot be reached, so a wrong URL or token shows up here rather than as an empty screensaver. Each failure carries a `reason` (#1909): `immich_not_configured` (400, URL or API key missing), `immich_api_key_rejected` (502, Immich answered 401 or 403), `immich_http_status` (502, any other error status, with `params.status`), `immich_unreachable` (502, no connection or timeout).

Admin-only endpoint.

parameters.name: X-CSRF-Token
parameters.description: Required for state-changing requests when using session/cookie authentication. Not required for API-token authentication.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Optional client-generated key (printable ASCII, max 255 chars) that makes this POST retry-safe. Repeating the request with the same key and the same body returns the original response with `Idempotent-Replayed: true` instead of creating a second record. Reusing a key for a different body, or retrying while the first attempt is still running, answers 409. Keys are stored for 24 hours and survive a restart.

get.description: Readable by every member, unlike the account endpoints: the recipes page shows "last synchronised" per account, and this answer never carries the API token. `lastError` is the raw message of the last failed sync or connection test, for logs and API clients. Since #1909 an account also carries `lastErrorReason` (string or null) and `lastErrorParams` (object or null): the case of that failure, which the settings page turns into its own sentence. The case is one of `recipe_providers_sync_auth_failed` (the provider answered 401 or 403), `recipe_providers_sync_wrong_url` (404, no provider API at this address), `recipe_providers_sync_http_status` (any other status, `params.status`), `recipe_providers_sync_timeout`, `recipe_providers_sync_unreachable` (DNS, refused or reset connection), `recipe_providers_sync_certificate` (the TLS certificate is not trusted), `recipe_providers_sync_bad_response` (unreadable or too large), `recipe_providers_private_network` (the address resolves to a private network and RECIPE_PROVIDER_ALLOW_PRIVATE_NETWORK is not set), or null when the failure has no known case. Both are null without `lastError`, and for a failure stored before the update until the next sync writes its case.

Modules, widgets, capabilities (including access levels and defaults), roles and the member list for the rights matrix. The catalog is the authoritative list of what can be granted - the enforcing side reads the same one, so the two cannot drift apart. defaults.capability is the legacy fallback; each capability item's default takes precedence when present. `childStart` lists what a new child account starts with in addition (modules and capabilities).

Admin-only endpoint.

get.summary: Get the stored rights of a role profile
get.description:
Only the deviations from the default are stored, so an empty answer means "this role uses the defaults", not "this role has nothing".

Admin-only endpoint.

parameters.name: familyRole
parameters.description: Family role the profile belongs to.

put.description:
Body: { modules, widgets, capabilities } - `modules` maps a module key to `none`, `read` or `write`, `widgets` maps a widget id to `none` or `allow`, and `capabilities` maps `notes_manage_household_categories`, `health_use_fasting`, `housekeeping_view_amounts`, `calendar_edit_others`, `notes_edit_others`, `inventory_edit_others`, `inventory_view_prices` and `tasks_reorder_family` to `none` or `allow`. Module and widget rows are replaced on every request. Capability rows are replaced only when `capabilities` is explicitly present, so older clients cannot silently remove them. Role values that match the default are not stored; a member-level `none` capability may be stored to override an inherited `allow`.

Admin-only endpoint.

put.summary: Replace the overrides of one member
put.description:
Body: { modules, widgets, capabilities } - `modules` maps a module key to `none`, `read` or `write`, `widgets` maps a widget id to `none` or `allow`, and `capabilities` maps `notes_manage_household_categories`, `health_use_fasting`, `housekeeping_view_amounts`, `calendar_edit_others`, `notes_edit_others`, `inventory_edit_others`, `inventory_view_prices` and `tasks_reorder_family` to `none` or `allow`. Module and widget rows are replaced on every request. Capability rows are replaced only when `capabilities` is explicitly present, so older clients cannot silently remove them. Role values that match the default are not stored; a member-level `none` capability may be stored to override an inherited `allow`. Each empty map means "inherit from the role" for that axis. To remove every override, send { modules: {}, widgets: {}, capabilities: {} }.

Admin-only endpoint.

Whole minutes as a number or digit string (`"1440"` = one day before), `"custom"` to use `reminder_custom_amount` and `reminder_custom_unit`, `""` for no reminder and no calendar event, or null for the day itself. On update, a value equal to the one already stored is accepted unchanged even if it lies outside these rules, so older records stay editable.

reminder_custom_unit.description: Unit for a custom lead time. Empty or null means unset (counted as days).

CalendarDateOrDateTime.description: A calendar date or date-time as stored and returned. Events created or edited through the API or the app carry household wall-clock time; events that came in through calendar sync (CalDAV, Google, Outlook, ICS) keep the instant they arrived with, including its Z or numeric offset.

oneOf.description: Yuvomi local wall-clock value in the household time zone, without offset.
Instant with Z or a numeric offset, as stored for a synchronized event. Returned unchanged.

CalendarDateOrDateTimeInput.description: A calendar date or date-time accepted by calendar mutations. What is stored is household wall-clock time: a value without offset is taken as such, a value with Z or a numeric offset is converted into the household time zone.

oneOf.description: Yuvomi local wall-clock value in the household time zone. Seconds and fractional seconds are optional and are dropped; stored as YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM.

UTC or numeric-offset input. Read as an instant and converted into household wall-clock time, stored as YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM - 2026-09-21T16:00:00Z in a Europe/Berlin household becomes 2026-09-21T18:00. For an all-day event only the date counts: the value is stored as its YYYY-MM-DD date as sent, so a midnight-UTC start stays on its day west of UTC. In the hour a DST change repeats, two instants map to the same wall-clock time; the stored value cannot tell them apart, so one of the two reads back an hour off.

is_series_start.description: Present on a row expanded from a series: 1 for its first occurrence.

color.description: The event's own colour as #RRGGBB, or null when it has none. Null is the normal state for an event nobody picked a colour for: it then borrows the colour of the first assigned member, and failing that cal_color. cal_color.description: Inherited colour of the source calendar or ICS subscription, read-only. Applies to every event of that source and therefore says nothing about this one; it is the fallback below color and the assignee.

local_calendar_id.description: Resolved local calendar for an authored event; null for generated or externally synchronized events and events with a Google/CalDAV target. Omit on create to resolve to the default without storing it. Membership applies to a whole series, never a single occurrence.

local_calendar_color.description: Colour of the local Yuvomi calendar, read-only. Used after event, assignee, and external source colours.

attachment_mime.description: Null when the event has no attachment or the caller may not read its document (see attachment_document_id).

attachment_size.description: Null when the event has no attachment or the caller may not read its document (see attachment_document_id).

attachment_document_id.description: The attachment's document in the Documents module. Null unless the caller may read that document: access to the Documents module (for API tokens a `documents:read` scope) and the document's own visibility. Without it the event carries no attachment at all - id, URLs, name, MIME type and size are null.

attachment_locked.description: True when the event has an attachment whose document the caller may not see (for example a private document of another member); it names nothing about that document, and such an attachment cannot be replaced or removed by this caller. attachment_data.description: Legacy attachment data URL. Null for attachments linked through attachment_document_id.

Up to v2.78.0 a timed occurrence was named by a `YYYY-MM-DD` day; linked occurrences stored before the change may still carry that form.

can_detach_occurrence.description: Legacy occurrence scopes for locally owned series that cannot use linked overrides, including outbound-synced and generated series.

max_upload_bytes.description: The largest upload this server accepts. Only with a valid credential, like `version`: before sign-in there is nothing to upload.

accepts_new_items.description: 0 on a list that mirrors a CalDAV reminder list which is read-only for its account.

ShoppingListChange.description: The change counter of a list around one write. When `before` equals the state a client holds, everything up to `after` is its own write. One write can move the counter by more than 1.

ShoppingItem.description: The fields from `external_uid` on are the bookkeeping of the CalDAV sync. They come with every item and a client has no use for them, so they are not required.

quantity.description: Free text, there is no separate unit.

category.description: The name of a shopping category.

price_cents.description: What was paid, in whole cents.

sort_order.description: Rank within the category of this list.

added_from_meal.description: The meal the item was transferred from.

external_source.description: `local`, or `caldav` on an item mirrored from a CalDAV list.

tags.description: The CATEGORIES of the mirrored CalDAV object, separate from `category`. Empty on a local item.

version.description: The change counter that belongs to exactly these items.

category.description: The name of an existing category, otherwise 400. Without it, `Sonstiges` while the household has that category, else the last one in shop order.

ShoppingItemUpdateInput.description: Every field is optional, and one that is not sent stays as it is. `name` and `quantity` have the limits of `ShoppingItemCreateInput`.

is_checked.description: true or false; 0 and 1 work as well, anything else answers 400. Responses carry 0 or 1.

category.description: The name of an existing category. It cannot be cleared.

price_cents.description: Whole cents. `null` or an empty string clears it, a string of digits is read as a number.

store_id.description: `null` or an empty string clears it, a string of digits is read as a number.

list_id.description: Moves the item to this list. `null` or the list it is on means no move, a string of digits is read as a number.

ids.description: Leaving the field out means every checked item. An empty array is refused with 400, not read as "all of them".

list_change.description: As in `ShoppingListChange`. `before` and `after` are null when the list does not exist.

avatar_data.description: PNG, JPEG, or WebP data URL.

access_scope.description: What kind of account this is, for example `family`, `split_guest` or `display`.

deactivated_at.description: Since when the account is deactivated, null for an active one.

changelog_seen.description: What the account last looked at in the changelog. Null means it never looked, which is another state than having seen everything.

version.description: The installed version at that moment.

latest.description: The last published version known at that moment.

birth_year_unknown.description: Only day and month of `birth_date` are known (#2095); the server then stores the placeholder year 2000 whatever year is sent. Without it, the stored flag only goes when a different date arrives.

onboarding_pending.description: Whether this account still needs the onboarding walkthrough. Derived from the account, not from the browser, so a new device does not repeat it. POST /auth/onboarding-seen clears it.

sso_only.description: Only present on GET /auth/users for administrators, and on GET /auth/me about the own account: the account carries no password and can only be entered through SSO.

sort_order.description: Position in the household member order, or null: for a member that has not been placed, and for every account that is no household member (staff, guest, deactivated).

is_household_member.description: Whether the account is a household member - the accounts GET /family/members lists and the only ones the member order takes.

order.description: The ids of all household members, in the wanted order.

householdSize.description: How many household members there are.

initialsRoster.description: The names a client resolves equal initials against. Empty for a split-expense guest.

othersCanRead.description: Modules another account can read too, which is when a privacy control means something.

csrfToken.description: Absent with a Bearer credential, which needs none.

sessionExpiresAt.description: When this browser session ends without further use, in milliseconds since the epoch. Absent with a Bearer credential.

gravatarHost.description: Host name of the service the operator configured in `GRAVATAR_BASE_URL` (e.g. `gravatar.com` or a Libravatar mirror), so the account page can name where the hash goes. Host name only - no scheme, port, path or credentials. `null` unless `gravatarAvailable` is true, and `null` when the configured value is not a valid public https URL.

language.description: Optional. Language code of a supported app locale (e.g. `de`, `pt`, `fil`). Sets the household data language (the language of server-generated titles such as birthday events), unless the automatic choice already yields it. Region, currency and date format are not derived from it. Unsupported values are rejected with 400; omitted, null or empty keeps the previous behaviour.

timezone.description: Optional. IANA time zone of the household (e.g. `Europe/Berlin`). Unknown zones are rejected with 400; omitted, null or empty keeps the fallback to TZ, the system zone and UTC.

sso_only.description: Create the account without a password, so it can only be entered through SSO. Requires OIDC to be configured, and rejects a password sent alongside it. Deliberately explicit rather than inferred from a missing password.

birth_year_unknown.description: Only day and month of `birth_date` are known (#2095); the server then stores the placeholder year 2000 whatever year is sent. Without it, the stored flag only goes when a different date arrives.

password.description: Write-only. Omit or leave empty to keep the current password.

sso_only.description: Switch the account between having a password and entering only through SSO. true clears the password; false requires a password to be sent with it, otherwise the account would be left with no way in at all. Omit to leave unchanged.

Invite.description: A pending invitation. The token hash is never returned.

username.description: Pre-assigned username. When null, the invited person picks one.

expires_at.description: Unix epoch milliseconds. Invitations are valid for 7 days.

username.description: Optional. When set, the invited person cannot choose a different one.

system_admin.description: Only true grants the admin role; the value is taken from the invitation, never from the accept request.

send_email.description: Send the invitation by email. Requires SMTP and BASE_URL; check email_sent in the response.

token.description: Plaintext invite token. Returned here and only here - the database holds nothing but its hash, so a lost token cannot be recovered, only revoked and reissued.

email_sent.description: Whether the invitation email actually went out. False when send_email was not requested, SMTP or BASE_URL is missing, or delivery failed - the link must then be passed on by hand.

invited_by.description: Display name of the member who created the invitation, or null when that account is gone.

username.description: Ignored when the invitation already carries one.

display_name.description: Ignored when the invitation already carries one.

subject_user_id.description: Family member whose identity, role, permissions, and data ownership apply to token requests.

scopes.description: Permission allow-list of "module:read"/"module:write" entries. null means no scoping (full role-based access, e.g. legacy tokens). write implies read.

active.description: Whether the token still signs in: not revoked and not past `expires_at`, judged by the server clock. Only a token with `active: false` can be removed.

subject_user_id.description: Optional family-member subject. Defaults to the administrator creating the token. Split-expense guests and wall displays are not eligible - neither can sign in, so neither may carry a credential beside its own.

scopes.description: Optional permission allow-list of "module:read"/"module:write" entries (e.g. ["calendar:write","tasks:read"]). Omit or null for a full-access token. When set, must be non-empty and only contain known scopes. Enforced on both REST and MCP; write implies read.

platform.description: A short lowercase name, for example `ios`.

current.description: Whether this device made the request.

device_id.description: Chosen by the client and stable per installation. Sending the same value again replaces the earlier credential.

credential.description: The device credential, shown once. Send it as a Bearer token.

ClientPermissions.description: The resolved rights of the account, for hiding what it cannot reach. The server enforces them either way. A device is an ordinary member here, also for an administrator.

modules.description: Per module key. Extension modules bring their own keys.

TwoFactorChallengeResponse.description: The password was right, but no session exists yet. Continue with POST /auth/2fa/verify in the same cookie session.

recoveryAvailable.description: Whether unused recovery codes are left.

code.description: The six-digit TOTP code or a recovery code.

householdSize.description: How many household members there are.

initialsRoster.description: The names a client resolves equal initials against. Empty for a split-expense guest.

othersCanRead.description: Modules another account can read too, which is when a privacy control means something.

guest_password_login_enabled.description: True only where password login is off and split-expense guests exist, who are exempt from the switch.

ReminderMoveNotice.description: A move of a shopping item that was taken back. The names are a snapshot of the moment.

back_list_id.description: Null once the list is gone.

entity_type.description: The origin of the reminder, for example `task` or `event`.

entity_title.description: Title of the entity, as far as the origin has one.

remind_at.description: As stored, and the form depends on who wrote the row: UTC without a zone suffix for a reminder set through this API, on rows from up to v2.68.0 possibly with an offset, and on derived types also `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM` or a UTC value with `Z` and possibly milliseconds. Parse it leniently; `GET /reminders/upcoming` has `fires_at` for scheduling.

assigned_from.description: Set on a reminder inherited from the person who created the entity.

cycle_anchor_kind.description: On `cycle_period`: whether this is the caller's own cycle or one passed on to a partner.

target_url.description: Only on `shopping_move_returned`, while the list still exists.

DashboardWeekEvent.description: An appointment in the compact shape of the week strip.

start_datetime.description: A date alone for an all-day appointment.

DashboardTask.description: A task of `urgentTasks`: the fields of `Task` without the picture of `assigned_to` and the tags.

description.description: Free text. Lines in the form `- [ ]` and `- [x]` are a checklist, see `PATCH /tasks/{id}/check`.

category.description: Key of a task category, see `GET /tasks/meta/options`. Categories are managed per household, so this is not a fixed list.

status.description: The state of the task. `archived` is not a status here: filing away is the separate axis `archived_at`.

start_date.description: `YYYY-MM-DD`, a plain calendar day without a time zone.

due_date.description: `YYYY-MM-DD`, a plain calendar day without a time zone.

assigned_to.description: The primary assignee, the first of `assigned_users`.

parent_task_id.description: Set on a subtask. There are at most two levels.

is_recurring.description: 1 when the task repeats, in the form 0 or 1.

recurrence_rule.description: RRULE of the series. A task synced over CalDAV may carry more than the vocabulary the API accepts.

recurrence_from_completion.description: 1 when the next occurrence counts from the day of completion instead of the due date.

recurrence_origin_id.description: The task this one followed in its series.

countdown.description: 1 when the task shows as a countdown.

locked.description: 1 when the definition of the task is closed to everyone but its creator and administrators (#830).

sort_order.description: Rank in the hand order of the category, null without a rank.

archived_at.description: UTC instant with `Z`, null while the task is not filed away.

created_at.description: UTC instant with `Z`, to the second.

updated_at.description: UTC instant with `Z`, to the second.

external_source.description: `caldav` for a task that lives on a CalDAV reminder list.

target_caldav_account_id.description: The reminder list a local task is sent to.

outbound_dirty.description: Bookkeeping of the sync; says nothing a client acts on.

outbound_attempts.description: Bookkeeping of the sync; says nothing a client acts on.

seen_on_server.description: Bookkeeping of the sync; says nothing a client acts on.

DashboardMeal.description: A paired wall display reads with `audience=household` and gets only the required fields.

listCount.description: Every selected list that exists, also beyond the three in `lists`.

DashboardBirthday.description: One occasion: a person with a birthday and a name day has two rows.

next_age.description: Null on a name day and when the year is unknown.

days_until.description: Negative within the grace period after the date.

series_id.description: Only on an appointment that replaces one occurrence.

recurrence_id.description: Only on an appointment that replaces one occurrence.

is_occurrence_override.description: Only on an appointment that replaces one occurrence.

assignment_owner_id.description: Only on an appointment that replaces one occurrence.

attachment_owner_id.description: Only on an appointment that replaces one occurrence.

reminder_owner_id.description: Only on an appointment that replaces one occurrence.

reminder_anchor_start.description: Only on an appointment that replaces one occurrence.

netMinor.description: In minor units, negative when the caller owes.

amount.description: The same value as a decimal string.
The same value as a decimal string.

view.description: `approver` sees every participant and all open requests, `self` only the own row and requests, `family` everybody by name without requests. Null without access to the module.

me.description: The caller. Missing without access to the module.

remaining.description: Null when the reward has no limit.

DashboardNutrientTarget.description: Null without targets. Null in a field means no target for this nutrient, which is another statement than a target of 0.

date.description: Null without access to the module.

presentSince.description: A check-in as stored, with milliseconds, so no `format`: a default ISO 8601 decoder refuses them.

unpaidAmount.description: Null for a caller who may not see amounts.

lastVisit.description: A check-in as stored, with milliseconds, so no `format`: a default ISO 8601 decoder refuses them.

todayItems.description: What expires today. A paired wall display gets the names only.

DashboardResponse.description: Every field listed here stays in the response without access to its module, in its empty form; only `shoppingTile` comes and goes. Depending on module access the response can carry further fields that are not listed here (at the moment `budget`, `health` and `fasting`): they are no part of this contract, and a client ignores what it does not know.

openTaskCount.description: Null when the count failed, which is not the same as none.

overdueTaskCount.description: Null when the count failed, which is not the same as none.

shoppingOpenCount.description: Null when the count failed, which is not the same as none.

pantryExpiring.description: Null when the read failed, which is not the same as nothing expiring.

OkResponse.description: The answer of a write that has nothing else to say.

server.description: The http(s) origin of this page, without a path. It goes into the link a client opens, and may take up to 170 characters once percent-encoded, so that the link still fits a QR code.

code.description: The code to type, shown once.

link.description: Opens the app on this device: `yuvomi://pair?server=<origin>&code=<code>`.

qr.description: The same link as a QR code, an SVG data URL.

code.description: Case, spaces and hyphens do not matter.

device_id.description: Chosen by the client and stable per installation. Sending the same value again replaces the earlier credential.

entity_title.description: Title of the entity, as far as the origin has one.

Parse it leniently; `GET /reminders/upcoming` has `fires_at` for scheduling.

assigned_from.description: Set on a reminder inherited from the person who created the entity.

cycle_anchor_kind.description: On `cycle_period`: whether this is the caller's own cycle or one passed on to a partner.

target_url.description: Only on `shopping_move_returned`, while the list still exists.

fires_at.description: The moment the reminder fires, in UTC with `Z`, whole seconds.

DmsAccount.description: A configured DMS account. The api_token is never returned; use has_token to check whether one is stored.

has_token.description: Whether an API token is stored for this account

api_token.description: API token for authenticating with the DMS. Write-only; never returned in responses.

DmsLinkResponse.description: The created family_documents row. storage_provider is `external` and storage_backend is `dms` for linked DMS documents.

ExtensionModuleWidget.description: Dashboard widget declared in a third-party module manifest.

entry.description: Protected asset URL for the widget JavaScript entry.

labelKey.description: Short i18n key resolved under extensions.{moduleId}.* (from locales/{locale}.json).

ExtensionModuleCapabilities.description: Normalized capabilities block from module.json (null when not declared or module errored).

apiPrefix.description: Sidecar API prefix. Must be exactly `/api/extensions/<module-id>`.

scopeKey.description: API token scope module key, typically `ext:<module-id>`.

settings.description: Optional settings sheet. sections controls visibility only; the module API enforces authorization.

entry.description: Protected module asset URL for the settings JavaScript entry.

sections.description: mine is visible to members; household only to administrators. No default.

i18n.description: Locale metadata scanned from locales/*.json in the module folder.

defaultLocale.description: Fallback locale when the UI language is not shipped (default en).

availableLocales.description: Locale files present in the module.

coreLocales.description: All locales supported by Yuvomi core.

manifestVersion.description: Manifest format version the module is written for (absent on errored modules).

entry.description: Entry file relative to the module folder (absent on errored modules).

style.description: Stylesheet relative to the module folder, or null.

page.description: Normalized page declaration (absent on errored modules).

ExtensionModuleInstall.description: How the module was installed from Settings (read from `.yuvomi-install.json` in its folder) and whether an admin has approved it since. null when the folder was copied onto the server by hand. Only present in the admin listing (`GET /api/v1/modules?admin=1` by an admin) and in install responses.

ref.description: Branch, tag or commit that was downloaded.

commit.description: Commit SHA of the GitHub archive, when known.

path.description: Folder inside the archive the module came from.

approved.description: False after every install and replace; true once an admin enabled the module from a browser session. While false the module is disabled whatever the household switch says, so a restored or fresh database cannot turn on code nobody looked at. Stored in the module folder.

installedByName.description: Display name of the admin who installed it, resolved from the user id in the record; null when that account no longer exists. Only in the admin listing.

writable.description: False when the modules folder is read-only; installs then answer 503.

persistent.description: Best-effort guess whether the modules folder survives an update of the server. False when Yuvomi runs in a container and the folder is not on a volume or bind mount (installed modules would be lost with the next image update); null when it cannot be determined. The routes still answer when false; the Settings page then shows the manual way, like for a read-only folder.

webInstall.description: Whether the operator switched installing from Settings on (`MODULES_ALLOW_WEB_INSTALL=true`). False by default; the install and delete routes then answer 403 `module_web_install_disabled`.

ref.description: Branch, tag or commit; overrides the ref from the URL.

path.description: Folder inside the repository that holds module.json. Overrides the folder of a tree URL; an empty string selects the repository root.

overwrite.description: Replace an installed module with the same id.

replaced.description: True when an installed module with the same id was replaced.

skipped.description: Files in the module folder that were not copied (not a web asset type, or a dotfile).

ModuleInstallResponse.description: The module is disabled either way, after a fresh install and after a replace: `data.install.approved` is false until an admin enables it from a browser session.

incoming.description: With `exists`: the module in the archive. A replace (retry with overwrite) always leaves the module disabled until it is approved again.

candidates.description: With `multiple`: the modules found in the archive.

resetAt.description: With `rate_limited` from GitHub, when GitHub names a time: when to try again (from `retry-after` for its secondary limit, otherwise from `x-ratelimit-reset`). Left out when GitHub names none.

weekdays.description: Comma-separated RRULE BYDAY codes (e.g. "MO,TH") for recurrence_kind=weekly; exactly ONE code (e.g. "MO") for recurrence_kind=monthly_ordinal_weekday. Null for monthly_fixed_day.

month_day.description: recurrence_kind=monthly_fixed_day: a day-of-month (1-31), or -1 for the last day. recurrence_kind=monthly_ordinal_weekday: the ORDINAL POSITION of the chosen weekday - -1 (last) or 1-4 (nth), reusing this same column for a different meaning (#1063 Phase 9). Null for weekly.

active.description: 0 = paused; contributes no occurrences until reactivated.

weekdays.description: weekly: an array of BYDAY codes, e.g. ["MO","TH"]. monthly_ordinal_weekday: a single code string, e.g. "MO".

month_day.description: monthly_fixed_day: 1-31 or -1. monthly_ordinal_weekday: the ordinal position, -1 (last) or 1-4 (nth).

replacement_date.description: null means this occurrence is explicitly skipped.
A date to move this occurrence to, or null to skip it.

original_summary.description: The imported event's own SUMMARY text; present when kind is "import".

coalesced.description: true when more than one origin (e.g. a schedule and a one-off) supplies this same date.

content_hash.description: sha256 of the ICS text behind the currently committed snapshot.

version.description: Bumped on every committed (re)import; the concurrency guard for reimport/commit.

last_success_at.description: Only updated on a successful commit; a failed attempt never clears it.

last_error.description: The English message of the last failed attempt, for logs and API consumers. Omitted for a caller without module write access, like url.

last_error_reason.description: The case of the last failed attempt (#1909): the same reason a manual refresh answers with (waste_source_fetch_http_status, waste_source_fetch_too_large, waste_source_fetch_blocked, waste_source_fetch_unreachable, waste_source_fetch_no_events, or the reason of a failed import). null when the attempt failed without a typed case, or before the first failure recorded after #1909. Omitted together with last_error.

last_error_params.description: The numbers of that case (status, limit_mb), as the refresh answer carries them in params. Omitted together with last_error.

needs_refresh.description: true when this source has no mapped pickup on or after today (invariant #6) - derived, not stored.

url.description: kind=url only. A credential: omitted entirely for a caller without module write access, never merely masked.

next_attempt_at.description: kind=url only. null while needs_mapping is set - the scheduler skips the source until a reviewed refresh.

consecutive_failures.description: kind=url only. Drives exponential backoff; reset to 0 on any successful fetch.

needs_mapping.description: kind=url only. Content changed but could not auto-commit (an unmapped label or unresolved blocking diagnostic); resolved only by a reviewed refresh.

type_ids.description: Every type this label maps to, ascending; one pickup per type is created for each of its entries. Empty when the label is ignored.

type_id.description: The lowest of type_ids, or null. Kept for callers from before a label could map to several types; read type_ids instead.

ignored.description: True exactly when type_ids is empty.

WasteSourceMappingUpdateInput.description: Either ignored: true, or the label's full new type set as type_ids (or a single type_id) - never both, and never type_id together with type_ids.

type_ids.description: Replaces the label's whole type set.

type_id.description: Shorthand for type_ids with one entry.

event_key.description: Present on a "blocking" diagnostic; pass it back in skip_event_keys on commit to exclude the affected event and unblock the rest of the file.

suggested_type_id.description: A same-name (case-insensitive) match against an existing type; a convenience default only, never applied on its own.

remembered_type_ids.description: Every type this label was mapped to on the source's last commit, on a re-import preview; empty otherwise.

remembered_type_id.description: The lowest of remembered_type_ids, or null. Kept for callers from before a label could map to several types.

digest.description: sha256 of what this preview shows (candidates/labels/diagnostics), not of the raw ICS bytes; pass it back as preview_digest on commit. A URL source may be re-fetched between preview and commit - this digest still matches as long as the parsed result is unchanged.

source_id.description: null for a fresh import preview.

expected_version.description: The source's current version, for a re-import preview; pass it back as expected_version on commit.

WasteImportMappingDecision.description: Either ignored: true, or at least one type: existing ones as type_ids (or a single type_id), a new_type to create inline, or both together. One decision is required per distinct label reported by the preview; each entry of a label becomes one pickup per type.

type_id.description: Shorthand for type_ids with one entry; not together with type_ids.

ics.description: The raw ICS file text (re-parsed on commit; never trusts a client-supplied candidate list).

name.description: Required for a fresh import (POST /import/commit); defaults to the existing name on a re-import.

skip_event_keys.description: Blocking-diagnostic event_key values explicitly acknowledged and excluded.

preview_digest.description: The digest returned by the matching preview; a mismatch (the parsed content actually changed since that preview) is refused with 409.

expected_version.description: Required on a re-import commit; the source's version as last seen in a preview (409 on mismatch).

coalesced.description: Informational: how many accepted pickups land on a date a manual schedule/one-off (or another source) already provides for the same type.

url.description: https:// only by default; http:// is accepted only under the operator opt-in WASTE_SOURCE_ALLOW_PRIVATE_NETWORK.

outcome.description: committed: every label had a remembered decision, applied via the same atomic path as a file re-import. unchanged: a conditional GET reported no change (304). needs_mapping: content changed but at least one label (or blocking diagnostic) has no remembered decision - see source.needs_mapping and the preview field. error: the fetch failed - see reason for its class and source.last_error for the stored message (source.last_error_reason keeps the same class for a later read).

reason.description: Only with outcome=error: the class of the failed fetch. http_status: the other side answered, but not with a success (params.status). too_large: the response exceeds the upload limit (params.limit_mb). blocked: a private or blocked address. unreachable: everything else (DNS, refused or reset connection, TLS, timeout, a redirect that is not followed). no_events: the other side answered with a success, but without a single calendar entry (a maintenance or login page, an empty calendar) - nothing is applied and the imported pickups stay (#1938). url_invalid / url_not_https: the stored URL no longer passes validation. Stored with the source as last_error_reason (and last_error_params) since #1909.

params.description: Only with a reason that carries a number: `{ "status": 404 }` or `{ "limit_mb": 5 }`.

type_name.description: Only present on GET (list); PUT's response is scoped to the one type_id already in the URL.

offset_days.description: Lead time before the pickup, in days. Bounded 0-14.

delivery_time.description: Household-local HH:MM the reminder is delivered at.

url.description: Public, unauthenticated .ics URL. Rotates when regenerated.

type_ids.description: Optional type selection. null (default) means every active type.
Waste type ids to include, or null to include every active type again.

pattern.description: Normalized source label this pattern matches.

source_name.description: Only present on export, informational only.

status.description: applicable: will be applied on commit. unchanged: source mapping already matches. unmatched_pattern: no mapping in this source has this pattern. unmatched_type: no waste type in this household has this name. ambiguous_type: more than one waste type shares this name and none of them is the mapping's own current type - never guessed at, resolve the name collision (rename one of the types) before this entry can apply.

profile_digest.description: Pass back unchanged on commit; a mismatch means the profile changed since this preview.
